# __5\. Context gaps and proposed rules__

## __5\.1 Context gaps__

Terms used in this PRD absent from the domain glossary\. __The glossary does not exist__, so this is its initial content\. Addressed to the Context Engineer \(A32\), __unassigned__ — OQ\-031\.

__Term__

__Proposed definition__

FCR

First Contact Resolution\. Definition contested; resolved as D\-005

CAB

Change Advisory Board\. Four types configured: Admin, Emergency, Infosec, IT

CMDB

Configuration Management Database\. Glossed incorrectly on call as "change management database"

ePHI

Electronically Protected Health Information\. Applicability to this product unestablished — OQ\-105

ITSM · SLA · RBAC

IT Service Management · Service Level Agreement · Role Based Access Control

Retrospective change request

A change raised after the work was performed, recorded for compliance

Grey period

The year between warranty expiry at year three and scheduled replacement at year four, during which repair cost falls on Celestial

In Store vs In Stock

In Store is sealed and new; In Stock is returned from a user\. Two distinct states, easily conflated

Base site

The default site applied to synced users\. Must be manually corrected after every sync today

Impact · Urgency · Priority

Impact is business reach; urgency is the requester's view; priority is derived from a matrix of the two

Pick Up

The action by which a technician self\-assigns an unassigned ticket

Back Out

A change\-implementation outcome that abandons the change and jumps to closure without verification

Resolved vs Closed

Resolved means a fix delivered pending requester confirmation; Closed is final

Monitoring \(status\)

A post\-change observation window\. __Not__ an incident status

OQ\-106__ is a logic defect inside __BR\-001__, not a preference\.__ As stated, business\-level impact resolves to High *regardless of urgency* — so an incident affecting the whole business at Critical urgency derives __High__, while one affecting a single department at Critical urgency derives __Critical__\. The more severe case gets the lower priority\. Visible in Diagram 3\. Flagged rather than silently corrected\. Recommended fix: Business × Critical → Critical\.

# __6\. Overview and purpose__

Celestial Systems runs its internal IT service desk on a licensed third\-party ITSM product on that vendor's top tier\. Ten or more modules are licensed; three are in active use — Request \(covering both service requests and incidents\), Change, and Asset \(EV\-004\)\.

This document specifies an internally built replacement: a web application through which employees raise requests and report incidents, IT technicians work and resolve them, and IT tracks the hardware and software estate\. It covers the full capability set observed across nine hours of requirements sessions, organised into ten module groups\.

__What this document asks its readers to decide\.__ Two things\. First, whether the specified behaviour is correct, complete and buildable — the five accepts in §3\. Second, and separately, __what to defer\.__ Everything evidenced is specified; nothing was phased out in advance\. Phasing is a collective decision to be taken on this document now that it is readable, not an editorial judgement made while writing it \(D\-003\)\.

# __7\. Problem and evidence__

## __7\.1 Why replace the incumbent__

__Driver__

__Corroboration__

__Weak end\-user customisation__ — changes the IT team wants cannot be made without vendor involvement \(EV\-002\)

~20 vendor\-predefined roles cannot be customised or even inspected \(EV\-187\)\. Vendor\-predefined statuses cannot be deleted, only worked around \(EV\-144\)

__A hard cap of 25 selections per operation__ against a need to act on 50 or more endpoints \(EV\-002\)

Scoped precisely at EV\-142 — applies to change requests as well as incidents and service requests

__Per\-technician seat licensing cost__ — eight licences held, one a read\-only developer account \(EV\-002, EV\-006\)

IT holds four members, Infosec four to five, ~nine seats\. Extending to Admin and HR would add more \(EV\-005\)\. The asset ceiling is a separate paid constraint — ~750 held, 670–680 consumed \(EV\-092\)

__Slow vendor support__ — roughly a day to raise a ticket, up to a week to resolve \(EV\-002\)

An attempted HR\-system integration failed and the vendor never completed it, so it was abandoned \(EV\-015\)\. The vendor declined to supply a list of module limitations \(EV\-032\)

The decision to build in\-house was taken at a Quarterly Business Review, with development planned for Q2 or Q3 \(EV\-003\)\.

## __7\.2 What the evidence does and does not support__

__Read this before treating any capability claim in §15 as settled\.__

One participant accounts for __41% of all utterances__ across the seven sessions and dominates six of the seven\. Almost every fact about the incumbent traces to one person's account of a product he administers\. No vendor was present at any session, and no second practitioner was available to contradict\.

__On the two occasions where a claim was independently tested, it failed\.__ Module export was denied five times across two sessions before the Architect found it in the settings \(CONF\-001\)\. The API was described as absent on 11 August and confirmed present on 12 August \(CONF\-002\)\. Those are the strongest available signals that current\-state claims here are under\-verified\.

Recorded as RISK\-001 and A\-006\. The deferred sandbox enumeration is the mechanism for verification, and G1 is deliberately held open for it\.

## __7\.3 Quantified pain — an honest gap__

No source states how many tickets are raised, how long they take, how often the 25\-item cap is actually hit, or what the customisation limitation costs in hours\. __Licence cost is the only quantified figure, and the business case rests on it alone\.__

Registered as OQ\-102 and RISK\-003\. It is the single most useful number anyone could add to this document\.

__The tension in __D\-001__, stated plainly\.__

The recorded words do not obviously support this reading\. EV\-167 says of change management that its *"existing workflow is very complicated and took two to three months to perfect, and that complexity must not be carried across\. The team should understand the workflow then design a simpler one\."* That is guidance about requirements, not about enumeration\.

D\-001 is nonetheless legitimate — the Product Manager holds Owner authority and the transcripts are the only requirements source available within C\-009's deadline\. But it is recorded as an interpretation with the conflict visible, and mirrored to §4 as OQ\-100, so the Sponsor reads a PRD specifying capabilities he said to simplify __and can see why\.__

__Partial mitigation already applied\.__ NG\-001 and NG\-002 honour the ruling directly: the interface is not reproduced, and §15\.4 specifies a five\-stage change workflow instead of eight, with the current flow retained as an appendix rather than as requirements\.

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.1 Incident Management__

__§15\.1 Incident Management__ — part of PRD · Internal Service Desk Tool · Full Scope \(ISDT\-PRD1\)

33 functional requirements · 6 use cases · 4 diagrams · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

## __Scope of this group__

An __incident__ is something broken — a password reset, a laptop performing poorly, Wi\-Fi failing\. It is distinguished from a service request, which is something new \(EV\-048\)\. The incumbent holds both as request types within one module; this PRD specifies them as separate groups \(D\-002\), because an incident goes straight to a form while a service request carries a second category\-selection step and an approval path \(EV\-060\)\.

This group covers intake through closure\. It does __not__ cover the service catalogue \(§15\.2\), the taxonomy and group definitions it consumes \(§15\.5\), the dashboard \(§15\.6\), the permission model \(§15\.7\), or the audit\-log surface \(§15\.8\)\.

## __Use cases__

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-001 · Report an incident through the portal__

__Actor__ Requester · __Precondition__ Signed in via organisation SSO \(C\-001\)

__Main success scenario__

1. Requester opens the portal and chooses to report a problem\.
2. Requester selects a category, then subcategory, then item as configured \(BR\-004\)\.
3. The form for that category renders\. Requester supplies a subject, a description, and any attachments\.
4. Requester selects urgency\. Impact defaults and may be adjusted\.
5. Requester submits\. The system derives priority, derives site from the user record, attaches the requester's assets, and returns a reference\.
6. Requester receives an email confirming the reference\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. No matching category exists → requester selects a general category and describes the problem freely; the gap is reported to the administrator\. 3a\. A mandatory field is empty → submission is refused with the field named\. 5a\. Requester's site is absent from the user record → the incident is created against the base site and flagged for correction\.

__Postcondition__ An incident exists with status Open, a derived priority, and a requester\-visible reference\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-002 · Report an incident by email__

__Actor__ Requester · __Precondition__ None — the requester need not be able to reach the portal \(EV\-198\)

__Main success scenario__

1. Requester emails the support mailbox\.
2. The system polls the mailbox and retrieves the message\.
3. The system checks the sender and subject against the exclusion filters\.
4. No ticket reference is present, so the system creates a new incident with intake mode Email\.
5. The sender address is matched to a user record and set as requester\.
6. Attachments are carried across\. The mail body becomes the description and opens a conversation thread\.
7. The system emails the requester the reference\.

__Extensions__ — 3a\. Sender or subject matches an exclusion filter → message discarded and logged, no incident created\. 4a\. Subject carries a reference to an existing incident → the message is appended to that incident's conversation and the assignee is notified\. 4b\. The referenced incident is Closed → it is reopened\. 5a\. Sender does not match any user → the incident is created unmatched and routed to a triage queue\.

__Postcondition__ Either an incident exists, or the message is discarded with a log entry\. No message is silently dropped\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-003 · Triage and assign an incident__

__Actor__ Technician · __Precondition__ At least one incident is unassigned

__Main success scenario__

1. Technician opens the unassigned queue\.
2. Technician reviews subject, category, priority and attached assets\.
3. Technician either picks the incident up, or assigns it to a named technician or group\.
4. The incident moves to In Progress and the assignee is notified\.

__Extensions__ — 3a\. The chosen technician is marked unavailable → assignment is refused, with the unavailability window shown\. 3b\. Several incidents are selected → all are assigned in one operation\. 3c\. The category is mapped to a technician → the incident never reached the queue; it was assigned on creation\. 4a\. The technician cannot resolve it → escalation to the next tier, recorded with a reason\.

__Postcondition__ The incident has exactly one assignee and status In Progress\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-004 · Work an incident to resolution__

__Actor__ Technician · __Precondition__ The incident is assigned to the technician

__Main success scenario__

1. Technician adds ordered tasks and, where useful, a checklist\.
2. Technician works each task, recording actual start and end\.
3. Technician records a resolution, optionally from a template\.
4. Technician sets status Resolved\.
5. The requester is notified that a fix has been delivered and asked to confirm\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. Progress depends on the requester → status Waiting for User; the SLA clock pauses\. 2b\. Progress depends on a third party → status Waiting for Vendor; the clock pauses\. 2c\. The requester withdraws → status Cancelled\. 3a\. The resolution field is empty → Resolved is refused\.

__Postcondition__ The incident is Resolved with a non\-empty resolution, or is paused or cancelled with a reason\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-005 · Confirm and close an incident__

__Actor__ Requester, then Technician · __Precondition__ Status is Resolved

__Main success scenario__

1. Requester confirms the fix\.
2. Technician completes the closure form — mandatory detail fields, first\-contact\-resolution flag, requester acknowledgement, closing comments, closure code\.
3. Status becomes Closed\.
4. The requester is notified of closure\.

__Extensions__ — 1a\. Requester does not respond within the auto\-close window → the incident closes automatically, recorded as closed without confirmation\. 1b\. Requester rejects the fix → status returns to In Progress with the original identifier and full history\. 2a\. A mandatory closure field is empty → closure is refused with the field named\.

__Postcondition__ Status is Closed with a complete closure record, or the incident is back In Progress\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-006 · Escalate an incident between tiers__

__Actor__ Technician · __Precondition__ The incident is assigned and In Progress

__Main success scenario__

1. Technician determines the incident is beyond their tier\.
2. Technician escalates, selecting the target tier and stating a reason\.
3. The incident is reassigned; the previous assignee is recorded in history\.
4. The new assignee is notified\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. No reason is given → escalation is refused\. 2b\. The target tier has no available technician → the incident is placed in that tier's queue rather than assigned\.

__Postcondition__ The incident sits with a technician at the target tier, and the escalation is traceable\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-001 to FR\-006 · Intake 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-001 · Portal intake form__

__Description__ The primary intake channel\. A requester reports an incident through a category\-specific form in the web portal\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Requesters need a route that captures enough structure for routing without forcing them to understand IT's taxonomy\. The incumbent offers this and it is the channel IT prefers \(EV\-010\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-010, EV\-052, EV\-059  
 __Priority__ P0 — no incident can be raised without an intake channel\. __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST render an incident form determined by the selected category, subcategory and item\.  
 The system MUST set intake mode to Web Form automatically and MUST NOT allow the requester to alter it \(EV\-052\)\.  
 The system MUST refuse submission where a field marked mandatory on that form is empty, naming each empty field\.  
 The system MUST return a reference visible to the requester on submission and MUST email the same reference\.  
 The system MUST accept attachments on the intake form\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-001 Given a requester on the portal with a category selected, when they submit a complete form, then exactly one incident is created with status Open and intake mode Web Form\.  
 AC\-002 *\(negative\)* Given a form with a mandatory description left empty, when the requester submits, then submission is refused, the description field is named, and no incident is created\.  
 AC\-003 Given a submitted incident, when the requester views their request list, then the reference returned on submission appears there\.  
 *Fixture* taxonomy\_seed\_min — one category, one subcategory, one item, with a form carrying one mandatory and one optional field\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield; see ADRs from the architecture gate\.  
 __UX requirements__ The form MUST NOT re\-render or lose entered data when the category selection changes at the subcategory or item level\. Attachment upload MUST show progress and MUST NOT block form entry\.  
 __Data and security__ Writes Ticket, Attachment\. Requester identity from session, never from a form field\. Description is free text and MUST be treated as Confidential \(§14\.1\)\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_created \{incident\_id, mode, category\_path, priority, site\} · incident\_form\_rejected \{reason, field\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-004, FR\-007, FR\-008 · __Blocked by__ none · __Design ref__ TBD — no design artefact exists \(OQ\-101\) · __Surface__ web  
 __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-001, AC\-002, AC\-003 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-002 · Email intake, create or update__

__Description__ An incident may be raised or updated by emailing the support mailbox\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Not everyone can reach the portal, and email intake is deliberately retained for that reason \(EV\-198\)\. Removing it would strand requesters who cannot log in\.  
 __Source__ EV\-010, EV\-198  
 __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-198\) · __Applies to__ UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST create an incident from a message carrying no recognised reference, setting intake mode to Email\.  
 The system MUST append a message carrying a recognised reference to that incident's conversation thread and MUST notify the current assignee\.  
 The system MUST match the sender address to a user record and set that user as requester\.  
 Where no user matches, the system MUST create the incident as unmatched and route it to a triage queue\. It MUST NOT discard the message and MUST NOT create a user record\.  
 The system MUST carry email attachments onto the incident\.  
 The system MUST reopen a Closed incident that receives a referenced message\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-004 Given a message from a known user with no reference in the subject, when polling runs, then one incident is created with mode Email and requester set to the matched user\.  
 AC\-005 Given a message whose subject carries the reference of an In Progress incident, when polling runs, then no new incident is created and the message appears on that incident's conversation thread\.  
 AC\-006 *\(negative\)* Given a message from an address matching no user record, when polling runs, then the incident is created with requester unmatched and no user record is created\.  
 AC\-007 Given a Closed incident, when a referenced message arrives, then its status becomes In Progress and the reopening is recorded in history\.  
 *Fixture* mailbox\_seed — four messages: known sender no reference, known sender with reference to open, unknown sender, known sender with reference to closed\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ The conversation thread MUST render the mail chain in chronological order and MUST distinguish inbound from outbound\.  
 __Data and security__ Writes Ticket, Attachment, History\. Sender address is PII\. An unmatched incident MUST NOT expose the raw sender address to requesters other than through the triage queue\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_created \{mode: email\} · incident\_email\_appended \{incident\_id\} · incident\_email\_unmatched \{\} · incident\_reopened \{incident\_id, trigger: email\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-003 · __Surface__ batch, web  
 __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-004, AC\-005, AC\-006, AC\-007 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-003 · Support mailbox configuration and polling__

__Description__ The mailbox the system watches, and how often\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Email intake is worthless if the mailbox is unwatched or the interval is too long to feel responsive\.  
 __Source__ EV\-197, EV\-010  
 __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-016 — interval conflicts across sources\) · __Applies to__ UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support Office 365 as the mail provider \(EV\-197\)\.  
 The system MUST poll the configured mailbox at an administrator\-set interval, defaulting to 60 seconds\.  
 The system MUST record every poll cycle with the count retrieved, including zero\.  
 The system MUST alert the administrator where polling fails on three consecutive cycles\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-008 Given the interval set to 60 seconds and a message arriving, when 90 seconds have elapsed, then the message has been retrieved and an incident exists\.  
 AC\-009 *\(failure\)* Given mail provider authentication failing, when three consecutive cycles fail, then an alert is raised to the administrator and the failure is recorded\.  
 *Fixture* mail\_provider\_stub — configurable to succeed or to reject authentication\.  
 *Verification* Integration test against a stubbed provider; interval measured from message receipt to incident creation\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ Not applicable — no user\-facing surface beyond the administrator configuration screen\.  
 __Data and security__ Mailbox credentials MUST be held as a secret reference, never as a value in configuration \(§21\)\. Applicable controls to be confirmed once the standards page exists\.  
 __Telemetry__ mailbox\_polled \{retrieved\_count, duration\_ms\} · mailbox\_poll\_failed \{error\_class\}  
 __Surface__ batch, admin  
 __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-008, AC\-009 → M\-004

CONF\-006__ unreconciled\.__ The polling interval was stated as 30–60 seconds on 12 August \(EV\-197\) and as 1–2 minutes on 3 August \(EV\-010\)\. Neither was reconciled on any call\. A 60\-second default is proposed as P\-016 with both sources cited, per D\-006\. Registered as OQ\-022 in the evidence pack\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-004 · Email exclusion filtering__

__Description__ Messages that must not become incidents — automated senders, test traffic, known noise\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The facility exists in the incumbent and is unused \(EV\-199\), but an unfiltered mailbox generates incidents from out\-of\-office replies and monitoring noise, which then need manual cancellation\.  
 __Source__ EV\-199  
 __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-019 — the administrator describes the capability but has never used it, so no working rule set exists\) · __Applies to__ UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to define exclusion rules matching sender address, subject keyword or body keyword\.  
 The system MUST discard a matching message without creating an incident, and MUST record the discard with the rule that matched\.  
 The system MUST NOT discard a message carrying a recognised incident reference, regardless of any matching rule\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-010 Given an exclusion rule on sender noreply@, when such a message arrives, then no incident is created and a discard entry names the rule\.  
 AC\-011 *\(negative\)* Given the same rule and a message from that sender carrying a valid incident reference, when polling runs, then the message is appended to the incident and is not discarded\.  
 *Fixture* mailbox\_seed\_filters — one exclusion rule, two messages, one carrying a reference\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ Discarded messages MUST be reviewable by an administrator for at least 30 days so a wrong rule is recoverable\.  
 __Data and security__ Discard log holds sender addresses — Confidential, PII\.  
 __Telemetry__ mailbox\_message\_discarded \{rule\_id\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-003 · __Surface__ batch, admin  
 __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-010, AC\-011 → M\-004

*Note: the incumbent also carries an "email command" toggle whose purpose the administrator does not know \(*EV\-199*\)\. It is not specified here — an unexplained capability is not a requirement\. Registered as *OQ\-107*\.*

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-005 · Requester site derivation__

__Description__ Every incident carries the requester's site, taken from the user record\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Site drives queue filtering, operational hours and cross\-site handover\. In the incumbent it auto\-populates and __cannot be corrected on the ticket__ — the user record must be fixed instead \(EV\-057\), and every directory\-synced user defaults to base site \(EV\-192\)\. That combination is the single largest source of administrator rework\.  
 __Source__ EV\-057, EV\-192 — both limitations  
 __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST derive site from the requester's user record at creation\.  
 The system MUST allow a technician holding the relevant permission to correct site __on the incident__, and MUST record the correction in history\. This is an improvement on the incumbent, which forbids it\.  
 Where the user record carries no site, the system MUST set base site and MUST flag the incident as site\-unconfirmed\.  
 The system MUST NOT block creation for a missing site\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-012 Given a requester whose record holds site Noida, when an incident is created, then the incident's site is Noida\.  
 AC\-013 Given an incident with a wrong site, when a permitted technician corrects it, then the incident's site changes and history records old value, new value, actor and timestamp\.  
 AC\-014 *\(negative\)* Given a technician without the permission, when they attempt to change site, then the change is refused and the incident is unaltered\.  
 AC\-015 *\(boundary\)* Given a requester whose record holds no site, when an incident is created, then site is base site and the site\-unconfirmed flag is set\.  
 *Fixture* users\_sites\_seed — one user per site plus one with no site\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ The site\-unconfirmed flag MUST be visible on the incident and in the queue, not buried in a detail tab\.  
 __Data and security__ Reads User, writes Ticket, History\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_site\_derived \{site, unconfirmed\} · incident\_site\_corrected \{from, to\}  
 __Prerequisites__ none · __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-004, C\-008 → AC\-012, AC\-013, AC\-014, AC\-015 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-006 · Automatic asset attachment__

__Description__ Assets held by the requester are attached to the incident automatically; the technician removes those not relevant\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The Executive Sponsor's stated rationale for asset management being in scope is that every ticket should associate with an asset so device tracking is not missed and the asset\-to\-issue correlation is available from the start \(EV\-170\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-058, EV\-170  
 __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-170\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST attach every asset currently assigned to the requester at creation\.  
 The system MUST allow a technician to remove an attached asset and to add one not automatically attached\.  
 The system MUST record every attach and detach in history\.  
 The system MUST NOT attach assets assigned to another user\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-016 Given a requester holding three assets, when an incident is created, then all three are attached\.  
 AC\-017 Given an incident with three attached assets, when the technician removes one, then two remain and history records the detach with actor\.  
 AC\-018 *\(negative\)* Given an asset assigned to a different user, when an incident is created for the requester, then that asset is not attached\.  
 *Fixture* assets\_seed — requester with three assets, second user with one\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ Where the requester holds more than five assets the list MUST be collapsible, so the incident form does not open dominated by hardware\.  
 __Data and security__ Reads Asset, writes Ticket\-Asset association, History\. BR\-002 means exactly one user per asset, so no shared\-ownership ambiguity arises\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_assets\_attached \{count\} · incident\_asset\_detached \{asset\_id\}  
 __Prerequisites__ §15\.3 asset records exist · __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-016, AC\-017, AC\-018 → M\-006

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-007 to FR\-012 · Priority and escalation 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-007 · Bulk selection ceiling__

__Description__ The maximum number of records selectable in one operation\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A hard cap of 25 against a need to act on 50 or more is one of the four stated drivers for replacing the incumbent \(EV\-002\), and it applies to incidents, service requests and change requests alike \(EV\-142\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-002, EV\-142  
 __Priority__ P1 — this is G\-002 in its entirety\. __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-020 — the need for 50\+ is sourced; the specific ceiling is not\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST permit at least 100 records to be selected and acted on in one operation\.  
 Where a bulk operation partially fails, the system MUST report which records succeeded and which failed, and MUST NOT roll back the successes silently\.  
 The system MUST NOT impose an undocumented ceiling\. Any ceiling MUST be configurable and MUST be stated to the user when reached\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-019 Given 100 incidents in the queue, when the technician selects all and assigns them, then all 100 are assigned in one operation\.  
 AC\-020 *\(failure\)* Given 100 selected where 3 are locked by another session, when bulk assignment runs, then 97 are assigned and the 3 failures are listed by reference\.  
 AC\-021 *\(boundary\)* Given the ceiling configured to 100 and 101 selected, when the technician acts, then the operation is refused with the ceiling stated numerically\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_bulk\_101 · *Verification* The 100\-record case runs within the FR\-030 latency budget\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ Select\-all MUST state how many records it selected\. Progress MUST be visible for operations exceeding two seconds\.  
 __Data and security__ Every record in a bulk operation MUST be permission\-checked individually\. A bulk action MUST NOT bypass per\-record authorisation\.  
 __Telemetry__ bulk\_operation \{action, requested\_count, succeeded\_count, failed\_count\}  
 __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-002 → AC\-019, AC\-020, AC\-021 → M\-002

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-008 · Impact and urgency capture__

__Description__ The two inputs from which priority is derived\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Impact is business reach as IT sees it; urgency is the requester's view\. Separating them lets priority be derived rather than argued \(EV\-054\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-054  
 __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ __Proposed__ in part \(P\-014 — impact values are sourced, urgency values are not\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST offer impact values Affects Business, Affects Department, Affects Group and Affects User \(EV\-054\)\.  
 The system MUST offer urgency values Critical, High, Medium and Low\.  
 The system MUST allow the requester to set urgency and MUST NOT allow the requester to set impact\.  
 The system MUST allow a technician to change both, recording the change\.  
 Both value sets MUST be configurable by an administrator \(G\-003\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-022 Given the intake form, when a requester views it, then all four urgency values are selectable and no impact control is present\.  
 AC\-023 Given an incident, when a technician changes impact from Affects User to Affects Department, then priority is re\-derived and history records both the impact change and the priority change\.  
 AC\-024 *\(negative\)* Given a requester viewing their own submitted incident, when they attempt to set impact through the API, then the request returns 403 and the incident is unaltered\.  
 *Fixture* priority\_matrix\_default — the matrix in Diagram 3\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ Urgency values MUST carry plain\-language help text; a requester should not need to know ITIL to choose one\.  
 __Data and security__ Writes Ticket, History\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_impact\_set \{value, actor\_role\} · incident\_urgency\_set \{value, actor\_role\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-009 · __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-003 → AC\-022, AC\-023, AC\-024 → M\-003

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-009 · Priority derivation matrix__

__Description__ Priority is computed from impact and urgency rather than chosen\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Removes per\-ticket negotiation and makes prioritisation auditable\. The incumbent does this on the vendor default matrix with no Celestial customisation \(EV\-054\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-054, EV\-055 · BR\-001  
 __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-014\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-002 · __See Diagram 3__

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST derive priority from the configured impact\-by\-urgency matrix at creation and on any change to either input\.  
 The system MUST apply BR\-001: any incident at Affects Business impact resolves to High regardless of urgency\.  
 The system MUST record the derived value, the inputs, and the matrix version used\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-025 Given impact Affects Group and urgency High, when the incident is created, then priority is Medium per the configured matrix\.  
 AC\-026 Given impact Affects Business and urgency Low, when the incident is created, then priority is High, demonstrating BR\-001\.  
 AC\-027 Given an incident with derived priority, when the matrix is later edited, then the existing incident's priority is unchanged and retains the matrix version under which it was derived\.  
 *Fixture* priority\_matrix\_default

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ The derived priority MUST show its inputs on hover or adjacent, so a requester can see why it is what it is\.  
 __Data and security__ Writes Ticket\. Matrix version is part of the incident record for audit\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_priority\_derived \{impact, urgency, priority, matrix\_version\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-008, FR\-010 · __Surface__ web, api, batch  
 __Traces__ G\-006, C\-002 → AC\-025, AC\-026, AC\-027 → M\-006

OQ\-106__ — a tension inside __BR\-001__\.__ As stated, business\-level impact resolves to High *regardless of urgency*\. That means an incident affecting the whole business at Critical urgency derives High, while an incident affecting one department at Critical urgency derives Critical — the more severe case gets the lower priority\. Flagged rather than silently corrected\. Recommended resolution: Affects Business × Critical urgency → Critical\. Owner: Product Owner \(A3\)\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-010 · Priority matrix configuration__

__Description__ An administrator can edit the matrix without a code change\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent runs the vendor default with no customisation possible in practice \(EV\-054\); weak customisation is a stated driver for replacement \(EV\-002\)\. This requirement is a direct instance of G\-003\.  
 __Source__ EV\-002, EV\-054  
 __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to set the priority resulting from each impact\-and\-urgency pair\.  
 The system MUST version the matrix and MUST retain superseded versions\.  
 The system MUST NOT re\-derive priority on existing incidents when the matrix changes\.  
 The system MUST refuse a matrix with any pair left unmapped\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-028 Given an administrator editing the matrix, when they change one cell and save, then a new matrix version exists and the prior version is retained\.  
 AC\-029 *\(negative\)* Given a matrix with one pair unmapped, when the administrator saves, then the save is refused and the unmapped pair is named\.  
 *Fixture* priority\_matrix\_default

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ The editor MUST present the matrix as a grid, not as a list of rules\.  
 __Data and security__ Administrator permission required\. Writes matrix version, History\.  
 __Telemetry__ priority\_matrix\_updated \{version, cells\_changed\}  
 __Surface__ admin  
 __Traces__ G\-003 → AC\-028, AC\-029 → M\-003

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-011 · Technician priority override__

__Description__ A technician may set a priority differing from the derived value\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent permits it \(EV\-056\) and judgement sometimes beats a matrix\. What the incumbent does not do is make the override visible as such\.  
 __Source__ EV\-056  
 __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a technician holding the relevant permission to set priority directly\.  
 The system MUST require a reason for the override and MUST refuse an override without one\.  
 The system MUST mark the incident as priority\-overridden and MUST show the derived value alongside\.  
 The system MUST NOT re\-derive priority over an override when impact or urgency later changes; it MUST instead flag that the inputs moved\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-030 Given a derived priority of Medium, when a technician overrides to High with a reason, then priority is High, the incident is marked overridden, and the derived value Medium remains visible\.  
 AC\-031 *\(negative\)* Given a technician overriding with an empty reason, when they save, then the override is refused and priority is unchanged\.  
 AC\-032 Given an overridden incident, when a technician later changes urgency, then priority remains the overridden value and the incident is flagged as inputs\-changed\.  
 *Fixture* priority\_matrix\_default

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ An overridden priority MUST be visually distinguishable from a derived one in both the incident and the queue\.  
 __Data and security__ Writes Ticket, History\. Override reason is Confidential\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_priority\_overridden \{from, to, actor\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-009 · __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-030, AC\-031, AC\-032 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-012 · VIP priority escalation__

__Description__ Incidents raised by a requester flagged VIP are raised in priority and routed to a senior tier\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent supports a VIP flag usable as workflow criteria, automatically raising priority to critical or high and routing to tier 3 or 4 \(EV\-024\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-024  
 __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-021 — the capability is described but the administrator did not state it is in use, nor who holds the flag\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-002

__Functional requirements__  
 Where the requester's record carries the VIP flag, the system MUST raise the derived priority by one level and MUST route the incident to the configured senior tier\.  
 The system MUST mark the incident as VIP\-escalated and MUST record the pre\-escalation priority\.  
 The escalation MUST be configurable and MUST be disableable entirely\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-033 Given a VIP requester and inputs deriving Medium, when the incident is created, then priority is High, the incident is marked VIP\-escalated, and the pre\-escalation value Medium is recorded\.  
 AC\-034 *\(negative\)* Given VIP escalation disabled, when a VIP requester raises an incident, then priority is the derived value and no escalation mark is set\.  
 AC\-035 *\(boundary\)* Given a VIP requester and inputs deriving Critical, when the incident is created, then priority remains Critical — escalation cannot exceed the top value\.  
 *Fixture* users\_vip\_seed — one VIP, one standard requester\.

__Technical requirements__ Not applicable — greenfield\.  
 __UX requirements__ VIP status MUST NOT be exposed to the requester on their own incident\.  
 __Data and security__ Reads User\.VIP — Confidential\. VIP flag MUST NOT appear in any requester\-visible surface or export\.  
 __Telemetry__ incident\_vip\_escalated \{from, to, target\_tier\}  
 __Prerequisites__ FR\-009, FR\-032 · __Surface__ web, api  
 __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-033, AC\-034, AC\-035 → M\-006

__FR\-013 to FR\-033 continue in the next increment__ — assignment and queue \(FR\-013 to FR\-018\), status and work \(FR\-019 to FR\-024\), resolution and closure \(FR\-025 to FR\-029\), SLA, history, tier escalation and cancellation \(FR\-030 to FR\-033\)\. Twelve of thirty\-three are published above\.

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.1 Incident Management \(continued\)__

__§15\.1 Incident Management — continued__ · ISDT\-PRD1

FR\-013 to FR\-033\. Part one \(PRD · ISDT · 15\.1 Incident Management\) carries the scope statement, six use cases, four diagrams, and FR\-001 to FR\-012\.

__Why this group is split\.__ Thirty\-three requirements at full block depth exceed what one authoring pass can produce\. The split is by capability cluster, not arbitrary — intake and priority in part one, assignment through closure here\.

__Diagram references corrected\.__ Diagrams 1–4 were regenerated on 17 August after a numbering defect: their FR labels had been produced before the numbering was final and were off by one from FR\-005 onward\. The attached images are the corrected versions\. If you attached earlier copies, replace them\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-013 to FR\-019 · Assignment and routing 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-013 · Unassigned queue__

__Description__ A shared queue holding every incident with no assignee\. In the incumbent, assignment is entirely manual and technicians poll this queue, including for cross\-site handover \(EV\-016\)\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Without a single visible queue, work is discovered by chance\. This is the technician's starting surface every morning\.  
 __Source__ EV\-016, EV\-069 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST place every incident with no assignee into the unassigned queue on creation\.  
 The system MUST remove an incident from the queue the moment an assignee is set, without a refresh\.  
 The system MUST allow filtering by site, priority, category and age\.  
 The system MUST show the age of each incident since creation\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-036 Given a newly created incident with no category mapping, when a technician opens the unassigned queue, then that incident appears with its age\.  
 AC\-037 Given an incident in the queue, when any technician assigns it, then it no longer appears in the queue for any other technician\.  
 AC\-038 *\(negative\)* Given an incident already assigned, when the queue is loaded, then it does not appear\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_queue\_seed — five unassigned across three sites, two assigned\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The queue MUST reflect assignment by another technician without a manual refresh, so two people do not pick up the same incident\. · __Data__ Reads Ticket\. Queue visibility is bounded by the requester\-visibility rules in §15\.7\. · __Telemetry__ queue\_viewed \{filter, result\_count\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-036, AC\-037, AC\-038 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-014 · Pick Up self\-assignment__

__Description__ A technician takes an unassigned incident for themselves in one action \(EV\-069\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-069 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a technician to assign an unassigned incident to themselves in a single action\.  
 The system MUST set status to In Progress on pick\-up\.  
 The system MUST refuse pick\-up where the incident has been assigned since the queue was loaded, and MUST state who holds it\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-039 Given an unassigned incident, when a technician picks it up, then they are the assignee and status is In Progress\.  
 AC\-040 *\(negative, concurrency\)* Given two technicians viewing the same unassigned incident, when both pick it up, then exactly one succeeds and the other is told who holds it\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_queue\_seed · *Verification* AC\-040 requires a concurrent test, not a sequential one\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Pick\-up MUST be reachable from the queue without opening the incident\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_picked\_up \{incident\_id, technician\_id, queue\_age\_sec\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-013 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-039, AC\-040 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-015 · Assignment to another technician or group__

__Description__ A technician assigns an incident to a named colleague or to a group queue\.  
 __Source__ EV\-016, EV\-018, EV\-062 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow assignment to a named technician or to a group\.  
 The system MUST notify the new assignee\.  
 The system MUST record the previous assignee in history on every reassignment\.  
 The technician selector MUST list every technician permitted to work incidents, and MUST NOT be limited by module tagging\. *This corrects the incumbent, where only technicians tagged to the module appear \(*EV\-062*, a limitation\)\.*

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-041 Given an assigned incident, when the technician reassigns it to a colleague, then the colleague is assignee and history records the prior holder\.  
 AC\-042 Given an incident assigned to a group, when a member of that group opens the group queue, then the incident appears there\.  
 AC\-043 *\(negative\)* Given a technician without incident\-work permission, when the selector is opened, then that technician is not listed\.  
 *Fixture* technicians\_groups\_seed — four technicians across two groups, one without permission\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The selector MUST show group membership and current open count per technician\. · __Data__ Reads Technician, Group; writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_assigned \{from, to, target\_type\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-019 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-041, AC\-042, AC\-043 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-016 · Bulk assignment__

__Description__ Several incidents assigned in one operation \(EV\-069\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-069, EV\-142 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a technician to select multiple incidents and assign them in one operation, subject to the ceiling in FR\-007\.  
 The system MUST apply the availability check in FR\-017 to a bulk assignment and MUST refuse the whole operation where the target is unavailable\.  
 The system MUST report per\-incident outcome where any individual assignment fails\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-044 Given 20 selected incidents and an available target, when bulk assignment runs, then all 20 are assigned and 20 history entries are written\.  
 AC\-045 *\(negative\)* Given 20 selected and a target marked unavailable, when bulk assignment runs, then none are assigned and the unavailability window is stated\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_bulk\_20, technicians\_availability\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Selection MUST survive pagination\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History — one entry per incident, never one for the batch\. · __Telemetry__ bulk\_operation \{action: assign, requested\_count, succeeded\_count\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-007, FR\-017 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-002 → AC\-044, AC\-045 → M\-002

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-017 · Technician availability and assignment check__

__Description__ Technicians can be marked unavailable over a date\-and\-time range; assigning to an unavailable technician raises an error \(EV\-012\)\. Unavailability is typed as leave or non\-leave \(EV\-013\)\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Prevents work landing with someone who cannot act on it — the commonest cause of an incident sitting untouched for a week\.  
 __Source__ EV\-012, EV\-013 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an unavailability record carrying start, end and type \(leave or non\-leave\)\.  
 The system MUST refuse assignment to a technician unavailable at the moment of assignment, stating the window\.  
 The system MUST show current availability in the technician selector\.  
 The system MUST NOT unassign incidents already held when unavailability begins; it MUST flag them for reassignment\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-046 Given a technician unavailable from today to Friday, when a colleague attempts assignment, then it is refused and the window is shown\.  
 AC\-047 Given a technician holding three incidents when unavailability begins, when the period starts, then all three remain assigned and are flagged for reassignment\.  
 AC\-048 *\(boundary\)* Given unavailability ending at 18:00, when assignment is attempted at 18:01, then it succeeds\.  
 *Fixture* technicians\_availability\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. *No calendar or directory integration is specified: the incumbent has none, an attempted integration failed and was abandoned \(*EV\-015*\)\.* · __UX__ Availability MUST be visible in the selector, not discoverable only on failure\. · __Data__ Reads Technician availability — Confidential; leave reason MUST NOT be exposed to other technicians\. · __Telemetry__ assignment\_refused \{reason: unavailable\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-046, AC\-047, AC\-048 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-018 · Category\-based auto\-assignment__

__Description__ A category may be mapped to a technician or group so matching incidents are assigned on creation \(EV\-061\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-061 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-022 — the capability exists in the incumbent and is *not used*, because all four IT members handle every category\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to map a category, subcategory or item to a technician or group\.  
 Where a mapping matches, the system MUST assign on creation and MUST NOT place the incident in the unassigned queue\.  
 Where the mapped technician is unavailable, the system MUST assign to their group, or to the unassigned queue where no group exists\.  
 Mapping MUST be optional; an unmapped taxonomy is valid\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-049 Given category Network mapped to a technician, when an incident is raised in that category, then it is assigned to them and skips the queue\.  
 AC\-050 Given the mapped technician unavailable, when such an incident is raised, then it is assigned to their group\.  
 AC\-051 *\(negative\)* Given an unmapped category, when an incident is raised, then it lands in the unassigned queue\.  
 *Fixture* taxonomy\_mapped\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Mapping MUST be editable on the taxonomy screen, not in a separate rules engine\. · __Data__ Reads Taxonomy node, Technician; writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_auto\_assigned \{category\_path, target\_type\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-013, FR\-017 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-049, AC\-050, AC\-051 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-019 · Support group routing__

__Description__ Groups defined by the nature of the ticket or the owning department — IT team, laptop, network, and a firewall group only Infosec may action \(EV\-018\)\. Group association determines which technicians a requester sees \(EV\-027\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-018, EV\-027 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-003

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an incident to be assigned to a group as well as to an individual\.  
 The system MUST restrict action on a group's incidents to members of that group and to administrators\.  
 The system MUST show a group queue to its members\.  
 A technician MAY belong to several groups\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-052 Given an incident assigned to the firewall group, when an Infosec member opens their group queue, then it appears\.  
 AC\-053 *\(negative\)* Given the same incident, when a non\-member technician attempts to pick it up, then the action is refused and the incident is unaltered\.  
 AC\-054 Given a technician in two groups, when they open group queues, then incidents from both appear\.  
 *Fixture* technicians\_groups\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Group membership MUST be visible on the technician's own profile\. · __Data__ Reads Group; writes Ticket\. Group definition itself belongs to §15\.5\. · __Telemetry__ group\_queue\_viewed \{group\_id, result\_count\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-052, AC\-053, AC\-054 → M\-006

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-020 to FR\-025 · Status and work 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-020 · Incident status model__

__Description__ The permitted statuses and the transitions between them\. __See Diagram 2\.__  
 __Use case and benefits__ Status is the primary signal of where an incident stands\. The incumbent carries nine statuses including two that belong to change management \(EV\-051\); this specifies a reduced set for incidents\.  
 __Source__ EV\-051 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-011 — the reduction is a design act\) · __Applies to__ UC\-004, UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support statuses Open, In Progress, Waiting for User, Waiting for Vendor, Resolved, Closed and Cancelled\.  
 The system MUST NOT permit a transition absent from Diagram 2\.  
 The system MUST treat Resolved and Closed as distinct: Resolved means a fix delivered pending requester confirmation \(EV\-051\)\.  
 The system MUST write a history entry on every transition, with no exception \(FR\-031\)\.  
 Monitoring MUST NOT be an incident status — it is a change\-management observation window\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-055 Given an incident In Progress, when the technician records a resolution, then status becomes Resolved and one history entry is written\.  
 AC\-056 *\(negative\)* Given an incident Open, when a transition directly to Closed is attempted through the API, then it is refused and status is unchanged\.  
 AC\-057 *\(negative\)* Given any incident, when Monitoring is set as status, then the request is refused — the value does not exist for incidents\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_status\_seed — one incident in each valid status\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Only legal next statuses MUST be offered; illegal ones MUST NOT be shown greyed\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_status\_changed \{from, to, actor\_role\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-055, AC\-056, AC\-057 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-021 · On\-hold reasons and SLA clock suspension__

__Description__ Two waiting states, distinguished by who is blocking, each pausing the SLA clock\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Without a pause, SLA figures measure the requester's or vendor's responsiveness rather than IT's, and the metric becomes unusable for the purpose it exists for\.  
 __Source__ EV\-051 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-012 — the pause behaviour is not stated in any source; it is inferred from the states existing\) · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST require a note when either waiting status is set\.  
 The system MUST suspend the SLA clock on entry to a waiting status and resume it on return to In Progress\.  
 The system MUST record cumulative paused duration separately from elapsed duration\.  
 The system MUST notify the requester when status becomes Waiting for User, stating what is needed\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-058 Given an incident with a 4\-hour SLA and 1 hour elapsed, when it sits Waiting for User for 24 hours and returns to In Progress, then 3 hours of SLA remain and paused duration reads 24 hours\.  
 AC\-059 *\(negative\)* Given a technician setting Waiting for Vendor with an empty note, when they save, then the change is refused\.  
 AC\-060 Given status becoming Waiting for User, when the transition completes, then the requester receives a notification naming what is required\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_sla\_seed · *Verification* AC\-058 requires clock manipulation in test, not real elapsed time\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Elapsed and paused durations MUST both be visible on the incident; one figure alone is misleading\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_paused \{reason\} · incident\_resumed \{paused\_duration\_sec\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-020, FR\-030 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-058, AC\-059, AC\-060 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-022 · Ordered tasks on an incident__

__Description__ An incident may carry multiple ordered tasks\. The worked example given for a damaged laptop display runs warranty check, raise an OEM ticket, schedule an engineer visit, then verify after replacement \(EV\-078\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-078, EV\-138 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow ordered tasks carrying title, description, own priority, owning group, status, scheduled start and end, actual start and end, and attachments\.  
 Task priority MUST be independent of incident priority \(EV\-078\)\.  
 Scheduled and actual times MUST be held separately and MUST NOT overwrite one another \(EV\-138\)\.  
 The system MUST NOT permit an incident to reach Resolved with an open task, and MUST name the open tasks when refusing\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-061 Given an incident with three ordered tasks, when the technician reorders them, then the new order persists and history records the change\.  
 AC\-062 *\(negative\)* Given an incident with one open task, when the technician sets Resolved, then it is refused and the open task is named\.  
 AC\-063 Given a task with a scheduled window, when actual start is recorded outside it, then both values are retained and the variance is visible\.  
 *Fixture* incident\_tasks\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Task completion percentage MUST derive from task status\. *The incumbent allows a closed request to read zero percent because tasks were never closed \(*EV\-138*\) — AC\-062 prevents that\.* · __Data__ Writes Task, History\. · __Telemetry__ task\_created · task\_completed \{duration\_vs\_scheduled\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-061, AC\-062, AC\-063 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-023 · Checklists__

__Description__ A freely definable checklist attached to an incident\. The facility exists in the incumbent, is not used, and the administrator suggested it would be useful in the new tool \(EV\-079\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-079 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-023 — a stated want from a proposal\-authority speaker, never used in practice\) · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a checklist of free\-text items, individually tickable, on an incident\.  
 The system MAY allow a checklist template attached to a category\.  
 Checklist completion MUST NOT block any status transition, unlike tasks\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-064 Given an incident with a five\-item checklist, when the technician ticks three, then completion reads 3 of 5 and each tick records actor and timestamp\.  
 AC\-065 Given an incident with an incomplete checklist, when the technician sets Resolved, then the transition succeeds — checklists are advisory\.  
 *Fixture* incident\_checklist\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A checklist MUST be visually distinct from tasks, since one blocks and the other does not\. · __Data__ Writes Checklist item, History\. · __Telemetry__ checklist\_item\_ticked · __Surface__ web · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-064, AC\-065 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-024 · Resolution recording__

__Description__ What was done, recorded before an incident may be Resolved\.  
 __Source__ EV\-051, EV\-089 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST require a non\-empty resolution before status may become Resolved\.  
 The system MUST record resolution author and timestamp\.  
 The system MUST make the resolution visible to the requester\.  
 The system MUST retain the resolution unchanged when an incident is reopened, and MUST require a new one before it may be Resolved again\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-066 Given an incident In Progress with a resolution entered, when the technician sets Resolved, then the transition succeeds and the requester can see the resolution\.  
 AC\-067 *\(negative\)* Given an empty resolution, when Resolved is attempted, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-068 Given a reopened incident, when the technician attempts Resolved without a new resolution, then it is refused and the prior resolution remains visible in history\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_status\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The resolution field MUST be prominent, not inside a collapsed panel\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. Resolution is free text and Confidential\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_resolved \{incident\_id, elapsed\_sec, paused\_sec\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-022 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-066, AC\-067, AC\-068 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-025 · Resolution templates__

__Description__ Reusable resolution text for recurring fixes\. Supported in the incumbent but none customised or used \(EV\-080\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-080 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-024 — capability described, never used\) · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to define named resolution templates\.  
 The system MUST allow a technician to insert a template into the resolution field and MUST allow editing after insertion\.  
 The system MUST record which template was used, where one was\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-069 Given a template exists, when a technician inserts and edits it, then the edited text is stored and the template is recorded as the origin\.  
 AC\-070 *\(negative\)* Given a template inserted and left unedited, when Resolved is set, then the transition succeeds — template text satisfies the non\-empty rule\.  
 *Fixture* resolution\_templates\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Insertion MUST NOT overwrite text already typed without confirmation\. · __Data__ Reads Template; writes Ticket\. · __Telemetry__ resolution\_template\_used \{template\_id, edited: bool\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-024 · __Surface__ web · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-069, AC\-070 → M\-004

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-026 to FR\-033 · Closure, SLA, history and cancellation 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-026 · Requester confirmation and reopening__

__Description__ Resolved awaits the requester's confirmation\. Confirmation leads to closure; rejection returns the incident to work\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The distinction between Resolved and Closed exists precisely so a fix is verified by the person who reported the problem \(EV\-051\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-051, EV\-089 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ in part \(P\-013 — the auto\-close window is unsourced\) · __Applies to__ UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST notify the requester on Resolved and MUST offer confirm and reject\.  
 On confirmation the system MUST permit closure\.  
 On rejection the system MUST return status to In Progress, retain the original identifier and full history, and require a reason\.  
 Where the requester does not respond within the configured window, the system MUST close automatically and MUST record closure as unconfirmed\.  
 The window MUST be configurable, defaulting to 5 working days\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-071 Given a Resolved incident, when the requester confirms, then closure becomes available and the confirmation is recorded with timestamp\.  
 AC\-072 Given a Resolved incident, when the requester rejects with a reason, then status is In Progress, the identifier is unchanged, and both resolution and rejection appear in history\.  
 AC\-073 *\(boundary\)* Given a Resolved incident and a 5\-working\-day window, when day 5 passes with no response, then status is Closed and the record shows closed\-without\-confirmation\.  
 AC\-074 *\(negative\)* Given a Resolved incident, when a user other than the requester or a technician attempts confirmation, then it is refused\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_resolved\_seed · *Verification* AC\-073 requires clock manipulation\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Confirm and reject MUST be actionable from the notification without a separate login journey\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_confirmed · incident\_reopened \{trigger: rejection\} · incident\_auto\_closed · __Prerequisites__ FR\-024 · __Surface__ web, api, batch · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-071, AC\-072, AC\-073, AC\-074 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-027 · Closure form and mandatory fields__

__Description__ Closure enforces completion of mandatory detail fields\. The incumbent's closure form carries a first\-contact\-resolution flag, a requester acknowledgement, closing comments and a closure code — the first three mandatory \(EV\-089\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-089 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST require first\-contact\-resolution flag, requester acknowledgement and closing comments before closure\.  
 The system MUST refuse closure naming each incomplete field\.  
 The system MUST require any field marked mandatory on the incident's category form to be complete before closure\.  
 Which fields are mandatory at closure MUST be configurable\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-075 Given a confirmed incident with all mandatory closure fields complete, when the technician closes it, then status is Closed and a closure record exists\.  
 AC\-076 *\(negative\)* Given closing comments left empty, when closure is attempted, then it is refused and that field is named\.  
 AC\-077 *\(negative\)* Given a mandatory category field left empty during work, when closure is attempted, then it is refused and the field is named\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_closure\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The closure form MUST show every outstanding field at once, not one at a time\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_closed \{fcr, acknowledged, closure\_code\} · closure\_refused \{field\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-026 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-075, AC\-076, AC\-077 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-028 · First contact resolution flag__

__Description__ Whether the incident was resolved at first contact\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A quality signal for the service desk\. Its definition was contested and is settled by D\-005\.  
 __Source__ EV\-089, EV\-090, EV\-091 · BR\-005 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-005\) · __Applies to__ UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST require the flag at closure\.  
 The system MUST apply D\-005: resolved in the first instance qualifies, and reaching out to the requester several times within that instance does not disqualify it\.  
 The system MUST apply BR\-005: a recurrence with a different root cause is a new incident and may be flagged; the same issue recurring may not\.  
 The system MUST show the definition inline at the point of entry\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-078 Given an incident with three requester contacts and one resolution instance, when the technician flags FCR true, then closure succeeds — multiple contacts do not disqualify\.  
 AC\-079 *\(negative\)* Given an incident reopened once and then resolved, when FCR true is set, then closure is refused with BR\-005 stated\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_fcr\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The D\-005 definition MUST appear beside the control, not in help documentation\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_closed \{fcr\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-027 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-078, AC\-079 → M\-006

CONF\-007__ resolved by __D\-005__\.__ The Owner's definition \(EV\-090\) is taken over the administrator's narrower reading \(EV\-091\)\. BR\-005's recurrence rule survives intact and is compatible with both\. Recorded rather than silently reconciled\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-029 · Closure codes__

__Description__ A coded outcome at closure\. Present in the incumbent and under\-used \(EV\-070, EV\-089\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-070, EV\-089 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-025 — no source enumerates the incident closure codes; the codes at EV\-136 belong to change management\) · __Applies to__ UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST offer a configurable closure code list\.  
 The system MUST require selection at closure\. *This differs from the incumbent, where the code exists but is not mandatory and is consequently unused\.*  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to add, rename and retire codes, and MUST NOT permit deletion of a code already used\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-080 Given a configured code list, when the technician closes an incident, then a code is required and stored\.  
 AC\-081 *\(negative\)* Given a code used on 12 closed incidents, when an administrator attempts deletion, then it is refused and retirement is offered instead\.  
 *Fixture* closure\_codes\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Retired codes MUST NOT appear for new closures but MUST still render on historical incidents\. · __Data__ Reads Closure code; writes Ticket\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_closed \{closure\_code\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-027 · __Surface__ web, admin · __Traces__ G\-003 → AC\-080, AC\-081 → M\-003

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-030 · SLA target assignment and breach detection__

__Description__ SLA targets are expressed as a date and time and settable in days, hours or minutes\. Not all tickets carry one \(EV\-011\)\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's dashboard carries both SLA\-violated and approaching\-violation widgets \(EV\-008\), so breach visibility is already part of how the desk is run\.  
 __Source__ EV\-008, EV\-011 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-026 — no source states the target values for any priority\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003, UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow SLA targets configured per priority, expressed in minutes, hours or days\.  
 The system MUST compute a due date at creation where a target applies, and MUST leave it empty where none does\.  
 The system MUST detect approaching breach at a configurable threshold and MUST notify the assignee and their group\.  
 The system MUST record breach without altering status — a breached incident is still workable\.  
 SLA elapsed time MUST honour operational hours and holidays \(C\-008\) and MUST exclude paused duration \(FR\-021\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-082 Given a High\-priority target of 4 hours and an incident raised at 16:00 with hours ending at 18:00, when 4 working hours elapse, then the due time falls at 11:00 the next working day\.  
 AC\-083 Given an 80% approaching\-breach threshold on a 4\-hour target, when 3 hours 12 minutes of working time elapse, then the assignee and group are notified once\.  
 AC\-084 *\(negative\)* Given a priority with no configured target, when an incident is created, then no due date is set and no breach can be raised\.  
 AC\-085 Given a breached incident, when a technician opens it, then it is fully workable and the breach is displayed\.  
 *Fixture* sla\_targets\_seed, calendar\_seed — operational hours and one holiday\. *Verification* Clock manipulation required\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Remaining SLA MUST be shown in working time, not wall\-clock, or the figure misleads\. · __Data__ Reads SLA target, calendar; writes Ticket\. · __Telemetry__ sla\_due\_computed · sla\_approaching · sla\_breached \{overdue\_sec\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-009, FR\-021 · __Surface__ web, api, batch · __Traces__ G\-006, C\-008 → AC\-082, AC\-083, AC\-084, AC\-085 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-031 · Incident history entries__

__Description__ Every change to an incident is recorded with actor and timestamp\. Named by the administrator as one of the mandatory sections to carry into the new tool \(EV\-088\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-068, EV\-087, EV\-088 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-088\) · __Applies to__ UC\-003, UC\-004, UC\-005

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST write a history entry for every field change, status transition, assignment, attachment and comment, recording target, actor, field, old value, new value, timestamp and operation\.  
 History MUST be append\-only\. No role, including administrator, may edit or delete an entry\.  
 History MUST be searchable and filterable by operation and by field \(EV\-087\)\.  
 An automated action MUST record the system as actor, never a person\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-086 Given an incident whose priority is changed, when history is opened, then an entry shows old value, new value, actor and timestamp\.  
 AC\-087 *\(negative\)* Given an administrator, when they attempt to delete a history entry through the API, then the request is refused and the entry is unaltered\.  
 AC\-088 Given an incident auto\-assigned by category mapping, when history is opened, then the actor is recorded as the system, not as a technician\.  
 AC\-089 Given history containing 40 entries, when filtered to status changes, then only status transitions are returned\.  
 *Fixture* incident\_history\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ History MUST default to most recent first and MUST NOT truncate silently\. · __Data__ Writes History — append\-only, Confidential, actor identity is PII\. This is expected to be the largest table in the system \(§14\.3\)\. · __Telemetry__ history\_viewed \{filter\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006, C\-002 → AC\-086, AC\-087, AC\-088, AC\-089 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-032 · Tier escalation__

__Description__ Escalation between support tiers\. The incumbent runs Tier 1 help desk, Tier 2 senior engineer or team lead, Tier 3 manager and Tier 4 director, with custom tiers creatable \(EV\-053\)\. L1 and L2 escalate when they cannot resolve \(EV\-069\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-053, EV\-069 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-027 — tier count conflicts, see below\) · __Applies to__ UC\-006

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a technician to escalate an incident to a higher tier, requiring a reason\.  
 The system MUST refuse escalation without a reason\.  
 Where no technician at the target tier is available, the system MUST place the incident in that tier's queue rather than assigning it\.  
 The system MUST record the escalating technician, the target tier and the reason in history\.  
 Tiers MUST be configurable, including adding tiers beyond the default set\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-090 Given a Tier 1 technician holding an incident, when they escalate to Tier 2 with a reason, then a Tier 2 technician is assignee and history records the escalation\.  
 AC\-091 *\(negative\)* Given an escalation attempt with an empty reason, when saved, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-092 Given no available technician at the target tier, when escalation occurs, then the incident sits in that tier's queue unassigned\.  
 *Fixture* tiers\_seed, technicians\_availability\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Escalation MUST be distinguishable from ordinary reassignment in both history and the incident view\. · __Data__ Reads Tier, Technician; writes Ticket, History\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_escalated \{from\_tier, to\_tier, reason\_length\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-015, FR\-017 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-090, AC\-091, AC\-092 → M\-004

CONF\-010__ unreconciled\.__ Four tiers were stated on 4 August \(EV\-053\) and five in session 7 on 12 August\. Neither was reconciled\. Four is proposed as P\-027 with both sources cited, per D\-006, and the requirement makes tiers configurable so the count is not baked in\. Registered as OQ\-023\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-033 · Cancellation__

__Description__ An incident withdrawn before resolution\.  
 __Source__ EV\-051 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-004

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow the requester to cancel their own incident before it reaches Resolved\.  
 The system MUST allow a technician to cancel with a reason\.  
 The system MUST require a reason in both cases\.  
 Cancelled MUST be terminal — a cancelled incident MUST NOT be reopened; a new incident is raised instead\.  
 The system MUST notify the assignee where one exists\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-093 Given an Open incident, when the requester cancels with a reason, then status is Cancelled and the reason is recorded\.  
 AC\-094 *\(negative\)* Given a Resolved incident, when the requester attempts cancellation, then it is refused — confirm or reject are the available actions\.  
 AC\-095 *\(negative\)* Given a Cancelled incident, when any actor attempts to return it to In Progress, then it is refused\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_status\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Cancellation MUST require explicit confirmation, since it is irreversible\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. __Reversibility__ irreversible\. · __Telemetry__ incident\_cancelled \{actor\_role, status\_at\_cancel\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-020 · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-093, AC\-094, AC\-095 → M\-006

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.2 Service Request Management__

__§15\.2 Service Request Management__ · ISDT\-PRD1

17 functional requirements \(FR\-034 – FR\-050\) · 4 use cases · 3 diagrams · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

## __Scope of this group__

A __service request__ covers something new — a laptop, an email account, VPN, a web category allowance — as distinct from an incident, which covers something broken \(EV\-048\)\. The incumbent holds three request types: Incident, Service Request and Request for Information \(EV\-049\)\.

Two things separate a service request from an incident and give this group its shape\. First, a service category carries a __second selection step__ — network, then request internet access — whereas an incident goes straight to its form \(EV\-060\)\. Second, service requests carry an __approval path__; incidents do not\.

Everything downstream of approval — assignment, tasks, resolution, closure, SLA, history — is shared with §15\.1 and is not restated here\. This group specifies the catalogue, the taxonomy that structures it, the templates that render it, and approvals\.
