__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-356 Given a new folder created at save time, when the catalogue is opened, then the folder and its report appear\.  
 AC\-357 *\(negative\)* Given a folder holding a private report, when a technician without access opens the folder, then the folder appears empty rather than hidden\.  
 *Fixture* reports\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ An empty\-looking folder MUST say it may contain reports the viewer cannot see, or it reads as a bug\. · __Data__ Writes Folder\. · __Telemetry__ report\_folder\_created · __Prerequisites__ FR\-119 · __Traces__ G\-003 → AC\-356, AC\-357 → M\-003

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-122 · Scheduled reports__

__Description__ Reports that run and arrive without anyone triggering them\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Scheduled reports can alert ahead of asset warranty or subscription expiry \(EV\-149\), and scheduled custom reports are one of the seven enumerated email triggers \(EV\-195\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-149, EV\-195 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-026

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow a saved report to be scheduled with a frequency and a recipient list\.  
 A recipient MUST NOT receive a report they could not read interactively\. __Scheduling MUST NOT be a route around visibility or scoping\.__  
 Each scheduled run MUST be recorded, including failures\.  
 The system MUST alert the schedule owner where a run fails twice consecutively\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-358 Given a report scheduled weekly to three permitted recipients, when the schedule fires, then all three receive it and the run is recorded\.  
 AC\-359 *\(negative\)* Given a recipient without permission to read the report, when they are added to the schedule, then it is refused and the reason is stated\.  
 AC\-360 *\(failure\)* Given two consecutive failed runs, when the second fails, then the schedule owner is alerted\.  
 *Fixture* reports\_scheduled\_seed · *Verification* Clock manipulation required\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The recipient list MUST show each recipient's read status, so a refusal is visible before saving\. · __Data__ Writes Schedule, run log\. Delivered content may contain PII\. · __Telemetry__ scheduled\_report\_sent \{recipients, row\_count\} · scheduled\_report\_failed · __Prerequisites__ FR\-119, FR\-127 · __Surface__ batch · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-358, AC\-359, AC\-360 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-123 · Drill\-down analysis__

__Description__ Reaching the records behind a figure \(EV\-149\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-149 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-027

__Functional requirements__  
 Any aggregate figure in a report or widget MUST be clickable through to the records composing it\.  
 The drilled list MUST honour row\-level scoping \(FR\-127\); a figure MUST NOT expose records the viewer cannot otherwise reach\.  
 Where scoping reduces the drilled list below the displayed aggregate, the system MUST say so rather than showing a mismatch silently\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-361 Given a widget showing 47 open tickets, when the viewer clicks it, then 47 records are listed\.  
 AC\-362 Given a viewer scoped to one site and an all\-sites aggregate of 47, when they drill in, then only their site's records list and the reduction is stated\.  
 AC\-363 *\(negative\)* Given a drilled record outside the viewer's scope, when they request it directly by ID, then it returns 403\.  
 *Fixture* reports\_scoping\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A count that does not match its drill\-down MUST explain itself; an unexplained mismatch destroys trust in every other figure\. · __Data__ Reads across modules\. · __Telemetry__ report\_drilldown \{aggregate, returned\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-127 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-361, AC\-362, AC\-363 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-124 · Dashboard and widgets__

__Description__ The operational view of the desk\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's Help Desk dashboard carries widgets for requests by technician, the unassigned queue, active tickets, open requests by mode, last week's inbound, completed and overdue, SLA violated, approaching SLA violation, open requests by priority, and a 20\-day received\-versus\-completed view \(EV\-008\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-008 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-027

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST provide a dashboard carrying at minimum the ten widget types at EV\-008\.  
 A widget MUST be addable, removable and repositionable by the viewer\.  
 A saved custom report MUST be exposable as a widget \(EV\-150\)\.  
 Every widget MUST support drill\-down \(FR\-123\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-364 Given the default dashboard, when a technician opens it, then the unassigned queue, active tickets, SLA violated and approaching\-violation widgets are present\.  
 AC\-365 Given a technician removing a widget, when they return the next day, then their layout persists\.  
 AC\-366 Given a saved custom report exposed as a widget, when the dashboard loads, then it renders with the viewer's scoping applied\.  
 *Fixture* dashboard\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The unassigned queue widget MUST be prominent by default; it is the technician's starting point every morning \(FR\-013\)\. · __Data__ Reads across modules\. · __Telemetry__ dashboard\_viewed \{widget\_count\} · widget\_added · __Prerequisites__ FR\-116, FR\-127 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-364, AC\-365, AC\-366 → M\-004

__The 20\-day received\-versus\-completed widget answers __OQ\-102__\.__ It is the one place in the incumbent that already holds ticket volume — the figure missing from §14\.3 and blocking every performance NFR\. One screenshot of it converts several proposals into facts\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-125 · Dashboard refresh__

__Description__ How dashboard figures become current\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Refresh frequency is configurable in the incumbent but is __set to never__, so refresh is manual \(EV\-009\)\. The AI Platform Lead argued against automatic refresh in an internal tool on server and network cost grounds, proposing a manual refresh button instead \(EV\-034\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-009, EV\-034 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-072 — EV\-034 is a proposal, and no interval is sourced\) · __Applies to__ UC\-027

__Functional requirements__  
 The dashboard MUST provide an explicit refresh control\.  
 The dashboard MUST show when its figures were last computed\.  
 Automatic refresh MUST be configurable and MUST default to off\.  
 A widget whose data is older than a configurable staleness threshold MUST indicate it\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-367 Given a loaded dashboard, when the viewer clicks refresh, then figures recompute and the last\-computed stamp updates\.  
 AC\-368 Given auto\-refresh off by default, when the dashboard sits open for an hour, then no background requests are issued\.  
 AC\-369 Given a 15\-minute staleness threshold, when figures are 20 minutes old, then each widget indicates staleness\.  
 *Fixture* dashboard\_seed · *Verification* AC\-368 is verified by network inspection, not by UI assertion\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A stale figure MUST look stale\. An SLA\-breach count that is silently an hour old is worse than no count\. · __Data__ Reads across modules\. · __Telemetry__ dashboard\_refreshed \{trigger: manual | auto, duration\_ms\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-124 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-367, AC\-368, AC\-369 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-126 · Dashboard site filter__

__Description__ Filtering the dashboard by site — Bangalore, Noida, non\-India, or all sites \(EV\-008\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-008, EV\-019 · C\-008 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-027

__Functional requirements__  
 The dashboard MUST be filterable by site and by all sites\.  
 The filter MUST default to the viewer's own site\.  
 The selection MUST persist across the session and across widgets\.  
 A viewer scoped to one site MUST NOT be offered all sites \(FR\-127\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-370 Given a Noida technician, when they open the dashboard, then it is filtered to Noida by default\.  
 AC\-371 Given a viewer selecting all sites, when they navigate away and return within the session, then all sites is still selected\.  
 AC\-372 *\(negative\)* Given a viewer scoped to Bangalore only, when the site filter is opened, then all sites is not offered\.  
 *Fixture* dashboard\_seed, sites\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The active site filter MUST be visible on every widget, or a filtered figure gets read as a global one\. · __Data__ Reads Site\. · __Telemetry__ dashboard\_site\_filtered \{site\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-105, FR\-124 · __Traces__ C\-008 → AC\-370, AC\-371, AC\-372 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-127 · Report data scoping__

__Description__ Which rows a reader may see, as distinct from which reports they may open\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Requester view permission has three settings — own requests only, all requests at their site, or all requests \(EV\-023\)\. A report must honour that\. Conflating report visibility with data scoping is how a shared report becomes a data\-leak path\.  
 __Source__ EV\-023, EV\-189 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-025, UC\-026, UC\-027

__Functional requirements__  
 Every report, widget, drill\-down and export MUST apply row\-level scoping based on the reader's role and view permission\.  
 Scoping MUST be enforced server\-side and MUST apply equally to the API\.  
 Two readers running the same report MUST see only the rows each is entitled to\.  
 Scoping MUST apply to scheduled deliveries, computed per recipient at send time \(FR\-122\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-373 Given one shared report and two readers scoped to different sites, when both run it, then each sees only their own site's rows\.  
 AC\-374 *\(negative\)* Given a reader scoped to own\-requests\-only, when they call the report API directly, then only their own records return\.  
 AC\-375 Given a scheduled report with two differently scoped recipients, when it sends, then each receives a differently scoped copy\.  
 AC\-376 *\(negative\)* Given an export, when run by a scoped reader, then out\-of\-scope rows are absent from the file\.  
 *Fixture* reports\_scoping\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Where scoping has reduced a result, the reader MUST be told, so an incomplete answer is not mistaken for a complete one\. · __Data__ Reads Role, User view permission\. Enforced server\-side\. · __Telemetry__ report\_scoped \{rows\_before, rows\_after\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-107 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-373, AC\-374, AC\-375, AC\-376 → M\-006

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.7 Authentication and Access__

__§15\.7 Authentication and Access__ · ISDT\-PRD1

13 functional requirements \(FR\-128 – FR\-140\) · 3 use cases · 1 diagram · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

## __Scope of this group__

Single sign\-on, session handling, and the enforcement of the permission model\. Role *definition* is §15\.5 \(FR\-107, FR\-108\); this group covers how those definitions are enforced, and how a person gets in at all\.

One decision shapes everything here\. The Executive Sponsor ruled that __Microsoft 365 authentication must be the single organisation\-wide mechanism__, that users must not hold multiple login identities or passwords, and that development must always use the organisation\-wide preferred choice \(EV\-181\)\. This system therefore holds no credentials at all\.

## __Use cases__

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-028 · Sign in__

__Actor__ Any user · __Precondition__ The user exists in the directory and is active

__Main success scenario__

1. The user opens the portal\.
2. The system redirects to Microsoft for authentication\.
3. Microsoft authenticates, applying whatever MFA policy the organisation has set\.
4. The user returns with an assertion and a session is established\.
5. The system applies role and scope for everything they subsequently see\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. The user is already signed in to Microsoft → they return without re\-entering anything\. 4a\. The assertion names a user this system does not hold → entry is refused and the attempt is logged; a record is __not__ created on the fly\. 4b\. The user is suspended or inactive → entry is refused with a reason distinguishing it from an authentication failure\.

__Postcondition__ A scoped session exists, or entry is refused with a logged, distinguishable reason\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-029 · Act within permission__

__Actor__ Technician · __Precondition__ A session exists

__Main success scenario__

1. The technician requests a record or an action\.
2. The system checks role permission for that module and action\.
3. The system checks row scope for that specific record\.
4. The action proceeds\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. The role lacks the action → refused, and no control was rendered for it\. 3a\. The record is out of scope → refused; the record is not disclosed to exist\. 4a\. The request arrives by API rather than interface → identical checks apply\.

__Postcondition__ The action is performed or refused on the same basis regardless of how it was requested\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-030 · Integrate a system by API__

__Actor__ A calling system · __Precondition__ A service identity exists

__Main success scenario__

1. The calling system authenticates as a named service identity\.
2. The system resolves that identity's role and scope\.
3. Requests are served within that role and scope\.
4. Every call is logged against the service identity\.

__Extensions__ — 1a\. No valid credential → 401\. 2a\. The service identity is suspended → 403\. 3a\. The call requests data outside scope → the same refusal a human would receive\.

__Postcondition__ Machine access is attributable and bounded by the same rules as human access\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-128 to FR\-134 · Sign\-in and sessions 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-128 · Single sign\-on__

__Description__ Authentication is delegated entirely to Microsoft Entra ID\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Authentication is configured at the identity\-management directory level rather than inside the application, using SAML with IDP login and logout URLs, server configuration and a certificate \(EV\-178\)\. The Owner ruled Microsoft 365 must be the single organisation\-wide mechanism \(EV\-181\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-178, EV\-181, EV\-182 · C\-001 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-181, Decision\) · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST authenticate users through Microsoft Entra ID using SAML\.  
 The system MUST accept an assertion only from the configured identity provider, validated against its certificate\.  
 Where an assertion names a user the system does not hold, entry MUST be refused and logged\. The system MUST NOT create a user record from an assertion\.  
 The system MUST NOT offer any alternative sign\-in path\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-377 Given an active synced user, when they open the portal, then they are redirected to Microsoft and return signed in\.  
 AC\-378 *\(negative\)* Given an assertion signed by an unconfigured provider, when it is presented, then entry is refused and the attempt is logged\.  
 AC\-379 *\(negative\)* Given a valid assertion for a person with no user record, when presented, then entry is refused and no user record is created\.  
 AC\-380 *\(negative\)* Given the sign\-in page, when inspected, then no username\-and\-password form exists\.  
 *Fixture* saml\_idp\_stub — configured and unconfigured providers\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield; the SAML library is an architecture decision\. · __UX__ The redirect MUST be immediate; a sign\-in page whose only control is a Microsoft button is a wasted step\. · __Data__ Reads User\. Assertion contents are Confidential and MUST NOT be logged in full\. · __Telemetry__ signin\_succeeded · signin\_refused \{reason\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-377, AC\-378, AC\-379, AC\-380 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-129 · Identity provider configuration__

__Description__ How the connection to the directory is configured and changed\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's configuration carries IDP login and logout URLs, server configuration and a certificate \(EV\-178\)\. It also displays a __live deprecation notice__ stating the setting is deprecated from the older directory \(EV\-179\) — a warning the Owner dismissed \(EV\-180\) and the Security Lead now owns\.  
 __Source__ EV\-178, EV\-179, EV\-180 · OQ\-011 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST allow an administrator to configure IDP login URL, logout URL, entity ID and signing certificate\.  
 The system MUST validate a new configuration against a test assertion __before__ it takes effect\.  
 The system MUST refuse a configuration change that would lock out every administrator\.  
 Certificate expiry MUST be surfaced ahead of time, on the same basis as warranty alerting \(FR\-058\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-381 Given a new IDP configuration, when saved, then it is validated against a test assertion before becoming active\.  
 AC\-382 *\(negative\)* Given a configuration that fails validation, when saved, then the previous configuration remains active\.  
 AC\-383 Given a signing certificate expiring in 30 days, when the alert job runs, then administrators are notified\.  
 *Fixture* saml\_idp\_stub

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The consequence of a bad configuration is total lockout; the validation step MUST NOT be skippable\. · __Data__ Certificate and endpoints\. The private side MUST be held as a secret reference\. · __Telemetry__ idp\_config\_updated · idp\_certificate\_expiring \{days\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-128 · __Surface__ admin · __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-381, AC\-382, AC\-383 → M\-006

OQ\-011__ is unresolved and sits directly under this requirement\.__ The administrator observed a deprecation notice on the authentication path in use and raised that the configuration may stop working \(EV\-179\)\. The Owner dismissed it as deprecated only in that path \(EV\-180\) — an assertion, not a vendor confirmation\. Per D\-007 this produces __no requirement__; it is a risk assessment owned by the Security Lead, not a specification of this product's behaviour\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-130 · No local credentials__

__Description__ This system holds no passwords and issues none\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The Owner ruled that users must not hold multiple login identities or passwords \(EV\-181\) and that a synced user must sign in seamlessly with no new or temporary password \(EV\-182\)\. That is a direct reversal of current behaviour, where an administrator activates each user and the tool emails a temporary password \(EV\-047\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-181, EV\-182 · C\-001, D\-004 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-182, Decision\) · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST NOT store a password, a password hash, or any local credential for a human user\.  
 The system MUST NOT provide a password reset, password change or forgotten\-password flow\.  
 The system MUST NOT send a credential by email\.  
 Service identities \(FR\-138\) are the sole exception and MUST use tokens, never passwords\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-384 *\(negative\)* Given the user schema, when inspected, then no password or hash column exists\.  
 AC\-385 *\(negative\)* Given the application routes, when enumerated, then no password\-reset endpoint exists\.  
 AC\-386 *\(negative\)* Given a newly synced user, when the outbound mail log is inspected, then no credential\-bearing message was sent\.  
 *Fixture* directory\_sync\_seed · *Verification* AC\-384 and AC\-385 are schema and route assertions in CI, not UI tests\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ No credential concept MUST appear anywhere in the interface\. · __Data__ Absence is the requirement\. · __Telemetry__ none\. · __Prerequisites__ FR\-128 · __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-384, AC\-385, AC\-386 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-131 · Session lifetime__

__Description__ How long a session lasts and how it renews\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent expires a session after roughly 24 hours, requiring daily login \(EV\-037\)\. No source states what Celestial wants\.  
 __Source__ EV\-037 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-081 — no target lifetime is sourced\) · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 Session lifetime MUST be configurable, defaulting to 12 hours of absolute life and 60 minutes of idle timeout\.  
 The system MUST re\-check access state \(FR\-101, FR\-113\) on renewal, not only at sign\-in\.  
 An expired session MUST return the user to the identity provider, not to an error\.  
 Session state MUST NOT be readable or forgeable client\-side\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-387 *\(boundary\)* Given a 60\-minute idle timeout, when a session is idle for 61 minutes and a request is made, then the user is returned to the identity provider\.  
 AC\-388 Given a user suspended after signing in, when their next request is made, then access is refused without waiting for session expiry\.  
 AC\-389 *\(negative\)* Given a tampered session token, when presented, then it is rejected and the attempt is logged\.  
 *Fixture* sessions\_seed · *Verification* Clock manipulation required for AC\-387\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Re\-authentication MUST return the user to where they were, not to the home page\. · __Data__ Session state, server\-side\. · __Telemetry__ session\_expired \{reason\} · session\_token\_rejected · __Prerequisites__ FR\-128 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-387, AC\-388, AC\-389 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-132 · Concurrent sessions__

__Description__ How many sessions a user may hold, and how many the system supports\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The administrator believes around 15 concurrent sessions are supported but states the __vendor has given no exact figure__ \(EV\-038\) — genuinely unobservable from outside, and registered as OQ\-009\. Separately the incumbent requires __separate browsers for the admin and user sessions__ \(EV\-039\), which is a workaround for a session\-scoping defect rather than a feature\.  
 __Source__ EV\-038, EV\-039 · OQ\-009 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-082\) · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 A user MUST be able to hold several concurrent sessions across devices\.  
 The system MUST NOT impose an arbitrary organisation\-wide concurrent\-session ceiling\. Capacity is governed by §14\.3 and §20, not by a licence\.  
 A user holding both administrative and non\-administrative capability MUST NOT need a separate browser to exercise either\. *This corrects *EV\-039*\.*  
 A user MUST be able to see and terminate their own active sessions\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-390 Given a user signed in on two devices, when they act on both, then both sessions function\.  
 AC\-391 *\(negative\)* Given an administrator in one browser tab, when they open a requester view in another tab, then both work without a second browser\.  
 AC\-392 Given a user viewing their active sessions, when they terminate one, then that session's next request is refused\.  
 *Fixture* sessions\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The session list MUST show device and last\-seen, or terminating the wrong one is inevitable\. · __Data__ Session state\. · __Telemetry__ session\_terminated \{by\_self\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-131 · __Traces__ G\-001 → AC\-390, AC\-391, AC\-392 → M\-001

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-133 · Multi\-factor authentication delegation__

__Description__ MFA is the identity provider's responsibility, not this system's\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent runs its own MFA with browser trust caching, and the trust duration is __contested across sources__ — 30 or 90 days at EV\-037, 180 days at EV\-039, same speaker, consecutive sessions \(CONF\-005, OQ\-021\)\. It also delivers the OTP to a distribution list \(EV\-037\), which defeats the purpose of a second factor\. Delegating to Microsoft removes all of this\.  
 __Source__ EV\-037, EV\-039, EV\-181 · OQ\-021 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-181, Decision\) · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST NOT implement its own multi\-factor authentication\.  
 The system MUST NOT hold or configure a browser\-trust duration\.  
 The system MUST NOT deliver a one\-time code by any channel\.  
 Where the organisation's policy requires step\-up authentication, the system MUST rely on the identity provider to enforce it\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-393 *\(negative\)* Given the application, when inspected, then no MFA configuration, OTP delivery or browser\-trust setting exists\.  
 AC\-394 Given an organisation MFA policy requiring a second factor, when a user signs in, then Microsoft prompts and this system is not involved\.  
 *Fixture* saml\_idp\_stub — with and without an MFA\-required policy\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ — · __Data__ None held\. · __Telemetry__ signin\_succeeded \{mfa\_asserted\} — recorded from the assertion, not enforced\. · __Prerequisites__ FR\-128 · __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-393, AC\-394 → M\-006

__This requirement dissolves __CONF\-005__ rather than resolving it\.__ Whether browser trust is 30, 90 or 180 days \(OQ\-021\) stops mattering once MFA belongs to Microsoft\. The conflict is recorded as unresolved in the evidence pack and is left there; it simply no longer bears on this product\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-134 · Sign\-out__

__Description__ Ending a session deliberately\.  
 __Source__ EV\-178 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-028

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST provide sign\-out, terminating the local session server\-side\.  
 Sign\-out MUST redirect to the identity provider's logout URL \(EV\-178\)\.  
 A terminated session MUST NOT be resumable by replaying its token\.  
 Sign\-out MUST be recorded\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-395 Given a signed\-in user, when they sign out, then the session ends and they are redirected to the provider logout URL\.  
 AC\-396 *\(negative\)* Given a signed\-out session token, when replayed, then it is rejected\.  
 *Fixture* sessions\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Sign\-out MUST be reachable in one action from every page\. · __Data__ Session state\. · __Telemetry__ signout · __Prerequisites__ FR\-131 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-395, AC\-396 → M\-006

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-135 to FR\-140 · Enforcement, scoping and machine access 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-135 · Server\-side permission enforcement__

__Description__ Every permission decision is made on the server\. __See Diagram 15\.__  
 __Use case and benefits__ RBAC is a stated mandatory element of Celestial's compliance regime \(EV\-189\)\. A control hidden in an interface is not a permission — it is a suggestion\.  
 __Source__ EV\-188, EV\-189 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-029

__Functional requirements__  
 Every read and every write MUST be permission\-checked server\-side\.  
 Hiding a control in the interface MUST NOT be the only enforcement of any permission\.  
 A refusal MUST NOT disclose the existence of a record the requester may not see\.  
 Enforcement MUST be identical across web, API, export and scheduled delivery\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-397 *\(negative\)* Given a technician whose role lacks asset edit, when they POST an asset update directly, then it returns 403 and the asset is unchanged\.  
 AC\-398 *\(negative\)* Given a record outside the requester's scope, when they request it by ID, then the response does not distinguish "not permitted" from "does not exist"\.  
 AC\-399 Given the same user and the same record, when requested through web, API and export, then all three produce the same decision\.  
 *Fixture* permissions\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A control the user may not use MUST NOT be rendered disabled; it MUST be absent\. · __Data__ Reads Role, User\. · __Telemetry__ permission\_denied \{module, action, surface\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-107 · __Surface__ web, api, batch · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-397, AC\-398, AC\-399 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-136 · Permission granularity__

__Description__ What a permission can be set on\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's matrix covers view, add, edit and delete per module across an access\-level section and a maintenance section, with advanced settings giving per\-action granularity \(EV\-188\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-188, EV\-193 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-029

__Functional requirements__  
 The matrix MUST support view, add, edit and delete per module\.  
 The system MUST support named per\-action permissions beyond the four verbs — for example export\-PII \(FR\-110\), read\-restricted\-attachment \(FR\-112\), and workflow override \(FR\-090\)\.  
 Permissions MUST be additive within a role; the system MUST NOT rely on ordering or precedence rules\.  
 Every named permission MUST appear in the role editor; there MUST be no hidden permissions\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-400 Given a role with asset view but not edit, when a holder opens an asset, then no edit control renders and a direct write returns 403\.  
 AC\-401 Given the export\-PII permission removed, when a holder exports, then PII columns are absent and a note says so\.  
 AC\-402 *\(negative\)* Given the role editor, when opened, then every permission the system enforces is listed and none is hidden\.  
 *Fixture* permissions\_seed · *Verification* AC\-402 compares the enforced permission set to the editor's list in CI\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Named permissions MUST carry a one\-line description; a checkbox labelled only with an identifier gets ticked at random\. · __Data__ Reads Role\. · __Telemetry__ permission\_granted \{permission\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-107, FR\-135 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-400, AC\-401, AC\-402 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-137 · Requester view permission__

__Description__ How much a requester can see\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Three settings exist: own requests only, all requests at their site, or all requests \(EV\-023\)\. This is the row\-scope gate for non\-technicians\.  
 __Source__ EV\-023 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-029

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support view scopes: own requests only, all at own site, and all requests\.  
 The default MUST be own requests only\.  
 Scope MUST apply to lists, search, reports, exports and the API identically \(FR\-127\)\.  
 A scope change MUST take effect on the next request, without requiring re\-authentication\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-403 Given a requester scoped to own requests, when they open their list, then only their own tickets return\.  
 AC\-404 Given a requester scoped to own site, when they open the list, then every ticket at that site returns and none from another site\.  
 AC\-405 *\(negative\)* Given a requester scoped to own requests, when they request a colleague's ticket by ID, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-406 Given a scope widened by an administrator, when the requester makes their next request, then the wider scope applies without re\-authentication\.  
 *Fixture* permissions\_seed, users\_sites\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A requester seeing colleagues' tickets MUST understand why; an unexplained wide scope reads as a privacy breach\. · __Data__ Reads User view permission\. · __Telemetry__ view\_scope\_applied \{scope, rows\_returned\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-135 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-403, AC\-404, AC\-405, AC\-406 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-138 · API authentication and authorisation__

__Description__ How a calling system gets in\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent exposes APIs covering each module and operation, and a tenant\-level API can be requested from the vendor using an organisation\-level privileged account \(EV\-183\)\. What APIs are available for Entra and Office 365 integration was asked on 4 August, deferred, and never covered \(OQ\-007\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-183, EV\-184 · OQ\-007 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-083 — no source states Celestial's own API requirements\) · __Applies to__ UC\-030

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support named service identities authenticating by token, not password\.  
 A service identity MUST hold a role and a scope, resolved on every call exactly as for a human \(FR\-135\)\.  
 Tokens MUST be revocable individually and MUST carry an expiry\.  
 Every API call MUST be logged against its service identity, and MUST be attributable in history as the system rather than as a person \(FR\-031\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-407 Given a service identity with ticket\-read scope, when it requests tickets, then only in\-scope tickets return\.  
 AC\-408 *\(negative\)* Given a revoked token, when presented, then it returns 401 and the attempt is logged\.  
 AC\-409 *\(negative\)* Given a service identity without asset write, when it POSTs an asset, then it returns 403\.  
 AC\-410 Given an API\-created ticket, when its history is opened, then the actor is the named service identity, not a person\.  
 *Fixture* service\_identities\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield; the token scheme is an architecture decision\. · __UX__ Token issuance MUST show the token once and never again\. · __Data__ Tokens MUST be stored hashed\. Call log is Confidential\. · __Telemetry__ api\_call \{identity, endpoint, status\} · token\_revoked · __Prerequisites__ FR\-135 · __Surface__ api · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-407, AC\-408, AC\-409, AC\-410 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-139 · Administrative boundary__

__Description__ What an administrator of this system can and cannot reach\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A useful precedent exists: the administrator's super\-admin rights cover the tool only\. The directory integration sits at organisation admin level, which he does not hold — so the integration walkthrough was __blocked on another person__ \(EV\-140\)\. That is a boundary working correctly, and it is retained rather than removed\.  
 __Source__ EV\-066, EV\-140 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-029

__Functional requirements__  
 An administrator of this system MUST NOT thereby hold any directory privilege\.  
 The system MUST NOT request or store directory\-administrative credentials\.  
 Actions requiring directory privilege MUST be identified as outside this system, naming what is needed\.  
 Administrative capability MUST be bounded per module where useful \(FR\-071\), not necessarily all\-or\-nothing\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-411 *\(negative\)* Given a system administrator, when they attempt an action requiring directory privilege, then it is refused and the required privilege is named\.  
 AC\-412 *\(negative\)* Given the configuration surface, when inspected, then no directory\-administrator credential is requested or stored\.  
 *Fixture* roles\_admin\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A refusal MUST say who can perform the action, not merely that the user cannot\. · __Data__ None additional\. · __Telemetry__ directory\_privilege\_required \{action\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-107 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-411, AC\-412 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-140 · Authentication and access audit__

__Description__ The record of who got in, who did not, and what changed about access\.  
 __Source__ EV\-068, EV\-189 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-028, UC\-029, UC\-030

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST log every sign\-in, every refused sign\-in with its reason, every sign\-out and every session termination\.  
 The system MUST log every permission denial with module, action and surface\.  
 The system MUST log every role assignment, permission change and scope change\.  
 The log MUST be append\-only and MUST be searchable by actor, date and outcome\.  
 The log MUST NOT record assertion contents or token values\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-413 Given a refused sign\-in, when the audit is searched by outcome, then it returns with its reason and timestamp\.  
 AC\-414 Given a role's permission changed, when the audit is opened, then the change, the actor and both values appear\.  
 AC\-415 *\(negative\)* Given any audit entry, when inspected, then no token value or full assertion is present\.  
 AC\-416 *\(negative\)* Given an administrator, when they attempt to delete an audit entry, then it is refused\.  
 *Fixture* audit\_seed, permissions\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Repeated refusals for one actor MUST be visible as a pattern, not only as individual rows\. · __Data__ Append\-only, Confidential\. Actor identity is PII\. · __Telemetry__ auth\_audit\_viewed \{filter\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-109 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-413, AC\-414, AC\-415, AC\-416 → M\-006

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.8 Notifications and Audit__

__§15\.8 Notifications and Audit__ · ISDT\-PRD1

12 functional requirements \(FR\-141 – FR\-152\) · 3 use cases · 1 diagram · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

## __Scope of this group__

Two cross\-cutting capabilities that every other module depends on\. __Notifications__ — what the system tells people, and when\. __Audit and history__ — the permanent record of what happened\.

The history log carries a direct instruction from the client\. It is named as one of the sections that __must be carried into the new tool__, recording every change with actor and timestamp across Request, Asset and Change \(EV\-088\)\. That makes it one of the few requirements in this PRD stated as a hard obligation rather than described as current behaviour\.

Inbound email is §15\.1 \(FR\-002, FR\-003, FR\-004\)\. This group covers outbound\.

## __Use cases__

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-031 · Be told something happened__

__Actor__ Any user · __Precondition__ An event occurs that concerns them

__Main success scenario__

1. An event fires — a ticket is created, assigned, resolved or closed; an asset is provisioned; a change transitions\.
2. The system resolves who the event concerns\.
3. Each recipient receives a notification carrying enough context to act without opening the system\.
4. The delivery is recorded\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. A recipient could not read the record interactively → they are not sent it\. 3a\. Delivery fails → the failure is recorded and retried, and persistent failure is surfaced to an administrator\. 3b\. Several events fire for one recipient in quick succession → they may be combined into one message if digesting is configured\.

__Postcondition__ Everyone who needed telling has been told, or the failure to tell them is visible\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-032 · Reconstruct what happened to a record__

__Actor__ Technician, Administrator or Auditor · __Precondition__ A record exists

__Main success scenario__

1. The reader opens the record's history\.
2. Every change appears with field, old value, new value, actor and timestamp\.
3. The reader filters by operation or by field to narrow it\.
4. The reader can answer who changed what, and when\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. A change was made by an automated process → the actor reads as the system, never as a person\. 2b\. The record has been anonymised → the actor reads as an anonymised token and the sequence is intact\. 3a\. The history is long → it pages rather than truncating\.

__Postcondition__ The full sequence is reconstructable by anyone entitled to read it\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-033 · Configure what the system sends__

__Actor__ Administrator · __Precondition__ Administrator permission

__Main success scenario__

1. Administrator opens the notification settings\.
2. Administrator enables or disables a trigger\.
3. Administrator edits the template for that trigger and previews it\.
4. Administrator saves; the change takes effect on the next event\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. Disabling a trigger would break a specified behaviour — such as the acknowledgement flow in FR\-068 — → the dependency is named and the change is refused\. 3a\. A template references a field that does not exist on that record → refused, with the field named\.

__Postcondition__ Notification behaviour matches what the organisation wants, without a code change\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-141 to FR\-146 · Notifications 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-141 · Notification triggers__

__Description__ The events that cause the system to tell someone\. __See Diagram 16\.__  
 __Use case and benefits__ Seven triggers are enumerated in the incumbent: a ticket created by portal or email, a technician assigned, a resolution added, a ticket closed, an asset provisioned or deprovisioned, every change stage or status transition, and scheduled custom reports \(EV\-195\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-195, EV\-149 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(D\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-031

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST fire notifications on all seven triggers at EV\-195\.  
 The system MUST additionally notify on an approval decision \(FR\-044\) and on SLA approaching or breached \(FR\-030\)\.  
 Each trigger MUST be independently enableable and disableable\.  
 Disabling a trigger that another requirement depends on MUST be refused with the dependency named\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-417 Given a ticket created through the portal, when creation completes, then the requester receives a notification carrying the reference\.  
 AC\-418 Given a change transitioning from Planning to CAB Evaluation, when the transition completes, then the change manager is notified\.  
 AC\-419 *\(negative\)* Given an administrator disabling the asset\-provisioned trigger, when they save, then it is refused because FR\-068's acknowledgement flow depends on it\.  
 AC\-420 *\(negative\)* Given a trigger disabled, when its event fires, then no notification is sent and no delivery record is created\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_triggers\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The settings page MUST show which requirements depend on each trigger, so disabling is an informed act\. · __Data__ Reads trigger configuration\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_triggered \{trigger, recipient\_count\} · __Surface__ batch, admin · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-417, AC\-418, AC\-419, AC\-420 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-142 · Notification templates__

__Description__ What a notification says\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A notification carrying only "your ticket was updated" forces the recipient into the system to find out what happened, which defeats the purpose\. Editable templates are also a direct instance of G\-003\.  
 __Source__ EV\-195, EV\-002 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-091 — no source describes the incumbent's template customisation\) · __Applies to__ UC\-033

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST hold an editable template per trigger, carrying subject and body\.  
 A template MUST support substitution of fields from the triggering record\.  
 The system MUST refuse a template referencing a field absent from that record type, naming the field\.  
 The system MUST preview a template against a sample record before it is saved\.  
 Templates MUST be versioned, and a sent notification MUST record the version used\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-421 Given a template referencing ticket reference and priority, when the notification sends, then both values appear substituted\.  
 AC\-422 *\(negative\)* Given a template referencing a field that does not exist on a ticket, when saved, then it is refused and the field is named\.  
 AC\-423 Given a template edited to version 2, when a notification sends, then the delivery record names version 2\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_templates\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Preview MUST render exactly what the recipient receives, including substitution\. · __Data__ Writes Template, History\. Templates may expose PII by substitution — see FR\-144\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_template\_saved \{trigger, version\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-141 · __Traces__ G\-003 → AC\-421, AC\-422, AC\-423 → M\-003

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-143 · Outbound mail configuration__

__Description__ How mail leaves the system\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's mail server configuration supports Outlook, Gmail and Office 365, and Celestial is on Office 365 \(EV\-197\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-197 · C\-001 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-033

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support Office 365 as the outbound mail provider\.  
 Credentials MUST be held as a secret reference, never as a configuration value\.  
 The system MUST validate the configuration by sending a test message before it takes effect\.  
 The system MUST alert an administrator where outbound delivery fails on three consecutive attempts\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-424 Given a valid Office 365 configuration, when a test message is sent, then it is delivered and the configuration activates\.  
 AC\-425 *\(negative\)* Given a configuration whose test message fails, when saved, then the previous configuration remains active\.  
 AC\-426 *\(failure\)* Given three consecutive outbound failures, when the third fails, then an administrator is alerted\.  
 *Fixture* mail\_provider\_stub — shared with FR\-003\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A mail outage MUST be visible in the interface, not only by absence of email\. · __Data__ Credentials as secret reference\. · __Telemetry__ mail\_sent · mail\_send\_failed \{error\_class\} · __Surface__ batch, admin · __Traces__ C\-001 → AC\-424, AC\-425, AC\-426 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-144 · Recipient resolution__

__Description__ Who gets told, and the check applied before they are\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ This is where EV\-084 went wrong: on an approval decision __only the technician is notified__, and the recorded response was to propose adding team addresses to a distribution list as a workaround \(EV\-085\)\. A distribution list also defeats per\-recipient permission checking — the same failure pattern as delivering an OTP to a list \(EV\-037\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-084, EV\-085, EV\-195 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-031

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST resolve recipients from the record — requester, assignee, group members, approver, change roles — rather than from a static list\.  
 The system MUST NOT send a notification to a recipient who could not read the underlying record \(FR\-135\)\.  
 The system MUST NOT rely on a distribution list as a substitute for resolving named recipients\.  
 Where a notification is suppressed because a recipient lacks permission, the suppression MUST be recorded\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-427 Given a ticket assigned to a group of four, when it is assigned, then all four group members are notified individually\.  
 AC\-428 *\(negative\)* Given a recipient whose scope excludes the record, when the notification would send, then it is suppressed and the suppression is recorded\.  
 AC\-429 *\(negative\)* Given the notification configuration, when inspected, then no static distribution\-list recipient can be set for a record\-derived trigger\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_recipients\_seed, permissions\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ An administrator MUST be able to see, for any record, exactly who would be notified by each trigger\. · __Data__ Reads User, Role, Group\. Recipient addresses are PII\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_suppressed \{reason\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-135, FR\-141 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-427, AC\-428, AC\-429 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-145 · Notification volume control__

__Description__ Preventing the system from becoming noise\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ EV\-195 fires a notification on __every__ change stage and status transition\. A change carrying twenty task updates and six transitions generates a great deal of mail, and a recipient who stops reading notifications is worse than one who never received them\.  
 __Source__ EV\-195 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-092 — no source raises volume as a problem; this is anticipated, not observed\) · __Applies to__ UC\-031

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support digesting several events for one recipient into a single message over a configurable window\.  
 Digesting MUST be configurable per trigger, and MUST default to off\.  
 Notifications carrying an action — approval, acknowledgement, confirmation — MUST NOT be digestible\.  
 A recipient MUST be able to see their own notification preferences\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-430 Given digesting enabled at 15 minutes for change transitions, when four transitions occur in ten minutes, then one message is sent listing all four\.  
 AC\-431 *\(negative\)* Given digesting enabled, when an approval request fires, then it sends immediately and is not digested\.  
 AC\-432 Given digesting off by default, when two events fire, then two messages are sent\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_triggers\_seed · *Verification* Clock manipulation required for AC\-430\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A digest MUST link to each underlying record, not summarise them into prose\. · __Data__ Writes digest queue\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_digested \{events\_combined\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-141 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-430, AC\-431, AC\-432 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-146 · Delivery record__

__Description__ Evidence that a notification was sent, or was not\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A notification that silently failed is indistinguishable from one nobody read\. Since approval, acknowledgement and confirmation flows all depend on a message arriving, the delivery record is what makes those flows auditable\.  
 __Source__ EV\-195, EV\-088 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-031

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST record every notification with trigger, recipient, template version, timestamp and outcome\.  
 A failed delivery MUST be retried on a bounded schedule and MUST be recorded as failed if retries exhaust\.  
 The delivery record MUST be visible on the record that triggered it\.  
 The record MUST NOT store the rendered message body where it would duplicate PII unnecessarily\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-433 Given a notification sent successfully, when the triggering ticket is opened, then the delivery appears with recipient and timestamp\.  
 AC\-434 *\(failure\)* Given a delivery that fails all retries, when the ticket is opened, then the delivery appears marked failed\.  
 AC\-435 *\(negative\)* Given a delivery record, when inspected, then it does not contain the rendered body\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_delivery\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A failed notification MUST be visible to the technician working the record, not only to an administrator\. · __Data__ Writes Delivery record\. Recipient address is PII\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_delivered · notification\_failed \{retries\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-141 · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-433, AC\-434, AC\-435 → M\-006

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-147 to FR\-152 · History and audit 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-147 · Unified history log__

__Description__ One append\-only record of every change, across every module\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ This is stated as an __obligation__, not a description: the history log is named as mandatory to carry into the new tool, recording every change with actor and timestamp across Request, Asset and Change \(EV\-088\)\. The auditor's recommendation to populate task and department detail for compliance evaluation \(EV\-139\) rests on it, and the revert facility \(EV\-068\) reads from it\.  
 __Source__ EV\-068, EV\-087, EV\-088, EV\-139 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-088, stated requirement\) · __Applies to__ UC\-032

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST write a history entry for every create, update, delete, state transition, assignment, attachment and comment, on every module\.  
 Each entry MUST carry target record, actor, field, old value, new value, timestamp and operation\.  
 An automated action MUST record the system or the named service identity as actor, never a person \(FR\-138\)\.  
 History MUST be written in the same transaction as the change it records, so a change cannot exist without its entry\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-436 Given a ticket priority change, when history is opened, then one entry shows field, both values, actor and timestamp\.  
 AC\-437 Given an asset reassignment, a change transition and a role edit, when each history is opened, then all three carry the same entry structure\.  
 AC\-438 *\(negative\)* Given a simulated failure writing the history entry, when a change is attempted, then the change is rolled back and does not persist\.  
 AC\-439 Given an auto\-assignment by category mapping, when history is opened, then the actor is the system\.  
 *Fixture* history\_seed · *Verification* AC\-438 requires fault injection, not a UI test\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. *Expected to be the largest table in the system \(§14\.3\), and its volume cannot be estimated until *OQ\-102* gives ticket volume\.* · __UX__ History MUST default to most recent first and MUST page rather than truncate\. · __Data__ Writes History — __append\-only__, Confidential, actor identity is PII\. · __Telemetry__ history\_written \{module, operation\} · __Surface__ web, api · __Traces__ G\-006, C\-002 → AC\-436, AC\-437, AC\-438, AC\-439 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-148 · History search and filtering__

__Description__ Finding the entry that matters\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's history is searchable and filterable by operation and by field \(EV\-087\)\. Without that, a long history is unusable — and history will be the largest table in the system\.  
 __Source__ EV\-087 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-032

__Functional requirements__  
 History MUST be filterable by operation, field, actor and date range\.  
 Filtering MUST be available on a single record's history and across a module\.  
 Cross\-module history search MUST honour row\-level scoping \(FR\-127\)\.  
 Results MUST state how many entries matched, distinguishing a scoped reduction from an empty result\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-440 Given a record with 60 history entries, when filtered to status changes, then only status transitions return with a count\.  
 AC\-441 Given a cross\-module search by actor, when run by a scoped reader, then only in\-scope entries return and the reduction is stated\.  
 AC\-442 *\(negative\)* Given a filter matching nothing, when run, then it reports zero matches rather than rendering an empty page\.  
 *Fixture* history\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The active filter MUST be visible above the results, or a filtered history reads as a complete one\. · __Data__ Reads History\. · __Telemetry__ history\_searched \{filters, matched\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-147, FR\-127 · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-440, AC\-441, AC\-442 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-149 · History immutability__

__Description__ No role may alter the record\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent permits a super admin to edit a closed change request \(EV\-137\), and the administrator states he will not do it\. FR\-090 removes that capability for change records; this requirement extends the principle to history itself, without exception\.  
 __Source__ EV\-088, EV\-137 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-032

__Functional requirements__  
 No role, including the highest administrative role, MAY edit or delete a history entry\.  
 No API endpoint MAY update or delete history\.  
 Retention\-driven removal, if ever introduced, MUST be a bounded archival operation that is itself recorded — never a silent delete\.  
 Anonymisation \(FR\-111\) MUST replace identity within history rather than removing entries\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-443 *\(negative\)* Given a super administrator, when they attempt to delete a history entry through the API, then it returns 403 and the entry is unaltered\.  
 AC\-444 *\(negative\)* Given the API surface, when enumerated, then no update or delete endpoint exists for history\.  
 AC\-445 Given an anonymised user, when their historical entries are opened, then the entries remain and the actor reads as an anonymised token\.  
 *Fixture* history\_seed, users\_anonymised\_seed · *Verification* AC\-444 is a route assertion in CI\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ No edit or delete control MUST appear on history for any role\. · __Data__ History — append\-only by construction\. · __Telemetry__ history\_mutation\_attempted \{actor\_role\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-147 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-443, AC\-444, AC\-445 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-150 · Configuration change audit__

__Description__ History for configuration, not only for records\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent holds a user activity audit through which unintended changes can be reverted \(EV\-068\)\. Configuration changes — taxonomy, roles, templates, SLA targets, the priority matrix — change how the system behaves for everyone, so they need the same traceability as a ticket\.  
 __Source__ EV\-068 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-032

__Functional requirements__  
 Every configuration change MUST write an audit entry — taxonomy, templates, roles, permissions, SLA targets, priority matrix, sites, calendars, notification settings\.  
 An entry MUST carry both values and the actor\.  
 Reversion \(FR\-109\) MUST be available on configuration and MUST record the reversion as a new entry\.  
 Configuration audit MUST be searchable alongside record history \(FR\-148\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-446 Given an SLA target changed from 4 to 2 hours, when the audit is opened, then the change, both values and the actor appear\.  
 AC\-447 Given a reverted configuration change, when the audit is opened, then both the original change and the reversion appear\.  
 AC\-448 *\(negative\)* Given a ticket field, when reversion is attempted on it, then reversion is not offered — it applies to configuration only\.  
 *Fixture* audit\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A configuration change with wide effect MUST state its blast radius before saving — for example how many templates a global change affects \(FR\-091\)\. · __Data__ Writes Audit\. · __Telemetry__ config\_changed \{area, field\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-147, FR\-109 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-446, AC\-447, AC\-448 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-151 · Notification and audit linkage__

__Description__ Connecting what happened to who was told\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Several specified flows turn on whether a message arrived — approval \(FR\-043\), asset acknowledgement \(FR\-068\), requester confirmation \(FR\-026\)\. Being able to show that the notification was sent, when, and to whom is what makes those flows defensible at audit\.  
 __Source__ EV\-088, EV\-195 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-093 — the linkage is designed, not observed\) · __Applies to__ UC\-031, UC\-032

__Functional requirements__  
 Each delivery record \(FR\-146\) MUST reference the history entry for the event that triggered it\.  
 From a history entry the system MUST show which notifications it caused and their outcomes\.  
 Where an action was taken in response to a notification, the resulting history entry MUST reference that delivery\.  
 A flow depending on a notification MUST be able to show whether it was delivered\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-449 Given an approval request notification, when the history entry for the approval is opened, then the delivery to the approver appears with its outcome\.  
 AC\-450 Given an asset acknowledgement, when the acknowledgement entry is opened, then the provisioning notification that prompted it is referenced\.  
 AC\-451 *\(failure\)* Given a failed approval notification and an approval never actioned, when the change is reviewed, then the failed delivery is visible as the reason\.  
 *Fixture* notification\_delivery\_seed, approvals\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ An outstanding approval whose notification failed MUST be distinguishable from one simply not yet actioned\. · __Data__ Reads Delivery record, History\. · __Telemetry__ notification\_action\_linked · __Prerequisites__ FR\-146, FR\-147 · __Traces__ G\-006 → AC\-449, AC\-450, AC\-451 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-152 · In\-application notification__

__Description__ Telling a signed\-in user without sending mail\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ No source describes an in\-application notification centre in the incumbent\. It is specified because several flows already need a signed\-in user's attention — an approval outstanding, an asset awaiting acknowledgement, a resolution awaiting confirmation — and email alone makes those invisible to someone already in the system\.  
 __Source__ Derived from FR\-026, FR\-043, FR\-068 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-094 — __no supporting evidence; designed from dependencies__\) · __Applies to__ UC\-031

__Functional requirements__  
 The system SHOULD present a signed\-in user the items awaiting their action — approvals, acknowledgements, confirmations\.  
 An in\-application notification MUST NOT replace the email notification for the same event\.  
 The list MUST be derived from record state, not from a separate notification store, so it cannot drift\.  
 Items MUST clear when the underlying action is taken, not by being dismissed\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-452 Given a user with two approvals outstanding, when they sign in, then both appear in their action list\.  
 AC\-453 Given an approval actioned, when the list is refreshed, then it no longer appears\.  
 AC\-454 *\(negative\)* Given an item in the list, when the user attempts to dismiss it without acting, then it is not dismissible\.  
 *Fixture* approvals\_seed, assets\_acknowledgement\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The list MUST be derived, not stored; a notification centre that can be marked read while the underlying work remains outstanding is worse than none\. · __Data__ Reads Approval, Asset, Ticket\. · __Telemetry__ action\_list\_viewed \{item\_count\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-141 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-452, AC\-453, AC\-454 → M\-004

Client / IT service owner

OQ\-142

Can notification templates be customised per trigger in the incumbent today? No source establishes this either way, so FR\-142 is proposed rather than approved\.

Client / IT service owner

OQ\-143

What is the history retention policy? FR\-149 forbids deletion, §14\.4 records that no policy exists, and history will be the largest table\. These three facts cannot all stay true indefinitely\.

Privacy / Data Protection \(A24\)

OQ\-144

Is an in\-application action list wanted at all? FR\-152 has __no supporting evidence__ — it is designed from what other requirements imply, and may be unnecessary if email suffices\.

Product Owner \(A3\)

__Two requirements here rest on no direct evidence\.__ FR\-145 \(volume control\) anticipates a problem no source reports\. FR\-152 \(in\-application notifications\) is derived entirely from what FR\-026, FR\-043 and FR\-068 imply\. Both are marked Proposed with that stated plainly — but they are the two most likely candidates for deletion at G2, and deleting them costs nothing downstream\.

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.9 Knowledge and Request for Information__

__§15\.9 Knowledge and Request for Information__ · ISDT\-PRD1

4 functional requirements \(FR\-153 – FR\-156\) · 1 use case · no diagram · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

__This is the smallest group in the PRD, and it is small honestly rather than by omission\.__

Two of its core requirements are already specified in §15\.2, where they belong: __FR\-047__ \(the Request for Information type\) and __FR\-048__ \(the policy and solutions catalogue\)\. They sit there because an RFI is a request type and the catalogue exists to deflect requests before they are raised\. They are cross\-referenced here, not duplicated\.

What remains is article lifecycle and measurement — four requirements, __all four proposals__, because the total available evidence for this area is two facts\.

## __The evidence, in full__

__Fact__

__What it says__

EV\-049

Request for Information is one of three request types and is __not in active use__\. The stated intention is to host AI usage policies and ISO, IT and network policy catalogues there for self\-service\.

EV\-050

The Solutions module exists in the incumbent but is __neither configured nor used__\.

That is the whole of it\. Nothing in nine hours of sessions describes article structure, ownership, review cadence, publishing workflow or effectiveness measurement\. The four requirements below are therefore designed from what a knowledge base needs in order not to rot — and every one of them is a candidate for deletion at G2 if the team decides a policy catalogue is enough\.

## __Use case__

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-034 · Publish and maintain a knowledge article__

__Actor__ Administrator or Technician · __Precondition__ Author permission

__Main success scenario__

1. The author drafts an article, or generates a draft from a ticket resolution\.
2. The article is reviewed by a named owner\.
3. The article is published and becomes visible to requesters \(FR\-048\)\.
4. The system records how often it is viewed and how often it deflects a request\.
5. At its review date the owner is prompted to confirm or revise it\.

__Extensions__ — 1a\. The source resolution contains customer or personal detail → it is flagged for redaction before publication\. 2a\. No owner is named → publication is refused\. 5a\. The review date passes without action → the article is marked stale and shown as such to readers\.

__Postcondition__ A published article has a named owner, a review date, and a measurable effect\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-153 to FR\-156 · Article lifecycle and measurement 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-153 · Article lifecycle__

__Description__ The states an article moves through: draft, in review, published, stale, retired\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent's Solutions module is __neither configured nor used__ \(EV\-050\)\. A knowledge base with no lifecycle is how that happens — articles are written once, never reviewed, and eventually nobody trusts them\.  
 __Source__ EV\-049, EV\-050 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-095 — no source describes any lifecycle\) · __Applies to__ UC\-034

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support article states draft, in review, published, stale and retired\.  
 Only a published article MUST be visible to requesters \(FR\-048\)\.  
 An article MUST NOT be publishable without a named owner and a review date\.  
 A retired article MUST remain readable through a direct link held by an existing ticket, and MUST NOT appear in search\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-455 Given a draft article, when a requester searches its exact title, then it does not return\.  
 AC\-456 *\(negative\)* Given an article with no owner named, when publication is attempted, then it is refused and the owner field is named\.  
 AC\-457 Given a retired article referenced by a closed ticket, when that ticket is opened, then the article still renders and is marked retired\.  
 *Fixture* policy\_catalogue\_seed — shared with FR\-048\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A stale article MUST be visibly stale to the reader, not silently served as current\. · __Data__ Writes Article, History\. Articles are Internal\. · __Telemetry__ article\_state\_changed \{from, to\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-048 · __Surface__ web, admin · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-455, AC\-456, AC\-457 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-154 · Authoring from a resolution__

__Description__ Turning a ticket resolution into a draft article\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Resolution templates exist in the incumbent and __none has been customised or used__ \(EV\-080\)\. The same fate awaits a knowledge base that requires someone to sit down and write articles from nothing\. The cheapest moment to capture an answer is when a technician has just written it\.  
 __Source__ EV\-049, EV\-080 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-096 — designed, not observed\) · __Applies to__ UC\-034

__Functional requirements__  
 A technician MUST be able to create a draft article from a ticket resolution in one action\.  
 The draft MUST carry a reference to the source ticket\.  
 The system MUST flag the draft for redaction review where the source resolution contains a field marked as personal data \(FR\-110\)\.  
 The draft MUST NOT be published automatically\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-458 Given a resolved ticket, when the technician creates an article from its resolution, then a draft exists carrying the resolution text and a reference to the ticket\.  
 AC\-459 *\(negative\)* Given a resolution containing a field marked personal, when a draft is created, then it is flagged for redaction and cannot be published until cleared\.  
 AC\-460 *\(negative\)* Given a draft created from a resolution, when it is created, then its state is draft and not published\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_resolved\_seed, policy\_catalogue\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The action MUST be offered at the point of resolution, not buried in a knowledge module the technician never opens\. · __Data__ Reads Ticket; writes Article\. __Resolution text may contain PII__ — hence the redaction flag\. · __Telemetry__ article\_drafted\_from\_resolution \{redaction\_flagged\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-024, FR\-110, FR\-153 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-458, AC\-459, AC\-460 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-155 · Deflection measurement__

__Description__ Whether the knowledge base actually prevents tickets\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ FR\-048 offers matching articles during catalogue selection, before a form is submitted\. Without measurement nobody can tell whether that works, and an unmeasured knowledge base cannot be justified or improved\.  
 __Source__ Derived from FR\-047, FR\-048 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-097 — no source asks for this\) · __Applies to__ UC\-034

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST record when an article is offered during catalogue selection and whether the requester then abandoned the form\.  
 The system MUST record article views separately from deflections\.  
 The system MUST report deflections per article\.  
 The system MUST NOT infer deflection from abandonment alone where no article was offered\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-461 Given an article offered during selection and the requester abandoning the form, when the deflection report runs, then one deflection is recorded against that article\.  
 AC\-462 *\(negative\)* Given a form abandoned with no article offered, when the report runs, then no deflection is recorded\.  
 AC\-463 Given an article viewed from search rather than during selection, when the report runs, then it counts as a view and not a deflection\.  
 *Fixture* policy\_catalogue\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ Deflection figures MUST be visible to the article owner, since they are the person who can act on them\. · __Data__ Writes article event records\. No PII\. · __Telemetry__ article\_offered · article\_deflected \{article\_id\} · article\_viewed · __Prerequisites__ FR\-048 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-461, AC\-462, AC\-463 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-156 · Review cadence and ownership__

__Description__ Keeping articles true\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The intended content is __policy__ — AI usage, ISO, IT and network policies \(EV\-049\)\. Policy changes, and a stale published policy is worse than no policy at all, because people act on it\.  
 __Source__ EV\-049 · __Priority__ P3 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-098 — OQ\-118 asks who owns the catalogue and at what cadence\) · __Applies to__ UC\-034

__Functional requirements__  
 Every published article MUST carry a named owner and a next\-review date\.  
 The system MUST notify the owner ahead of the review date \(FR\-141\)\.  
 An article past its review date MUST be marked stale and MUST be shown as stale to readers\.  
 A stale article MUST remain readable; staleness MUST NOT hide it, because a stale policy is still the last known policy\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-464 Given an article with a review date in 14 days and a 30\-day lead time, when the notification job runs, then the owner is notified once\.  
 AC\-465 *\(boundary\)* Given an article whose review date passed yesterday, when a requester opens it, then it renders marked stale\.  
 AC\-466 *\(negative\)* Given a stale article, when a requester searches for it, then it still returns, marked stale\.  
 *Fixture* policy\_catalogue\_seed · *Verification* Clock manipulation required\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The staleness marker MUST state the review date, so the reader can judge how stale\. · __Data__ Writes Article\. Owner identity is PII\. · __Telemetry__ article\_review\_due · article\_marked\_stale · __Prerequisites__ FR\-141, FR\-153 · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-464, AC\-465, AC\-466 → M\-004

# __PRD · ISDT · 15\.10 Data Migration and Import Export__

__§15\.10 Data Migration and Import / Export__ · ISDT\-PRD1

7 functional requirements \(FR\-157 – FR\-163\) · 3 use cases · 1 diagram · all traced to ISDT\-PRD1\-EVP\-001

## __Scope of this group__

The __product capability__ to get data in and out\. Per the shed list this group deliberately excludes the migration *project* — the tenant API request, the extraction method, cutover sequencing and rollback rehearsal are execution, owned by the Data Architect, and only the end state is retained here\.

Entity\-specific import and export are already specified where they belong: __FR\-037__ taxonomy \(§15\.2\), __FR\-070__ assets and software \(§15\.3\), __FR\-099__ user archival \(§15\.5\), __FR\-118__ export completeness \(§15\.6\)\. This group specifies the __common framework__ those requirements share, plus the two things nothing else covers: ticket history and attachments\.

__This group is blocked on two of the evidence pack's blocking open questions\.__ OQ\-002 — whether a tenant\-scoped API will be granted, what it exposes, and what is needed to enable it\. OQ\-003 — the optimal migration route for Help Desk and Change data carrying resolutions and email conversations\. FR\-160 and FR\-161 cannot be built until both are answered\. __See Diagram 18\.__
