## __The one thing that genuinely matters__

The Frontend Engineer's scope statement is the clearest sentence in nine hours of evidence on this subject: __the one thing genuinely needed from the old tool is asset data, because it cannot be re\-entered by hand__ \(EV\-186\)\. Roughly 670–680 records \(EV\-092\)\.

Everything else is negotiable\. The administrator himself noted that module export may suffice for assets specifically but __not__ for Help Desk and Change, because resolutions and email conversations do not come across \(EV\-185\)\. If OQ\-002 and OQ\-003 resolve unfavourably, the fallback — migrate assets, start ticket history fresh — is a real and acceptable option\. It should be *chosen*, not defaulted into by running out of time\.

CONF\-001__ is the warning that hangs over this whole group\.__ Module export was denied five times across two sessions before the Architect found it in the settings\. A capability that exists was very nearly recorded as absent\. Every capability claim about the incumbent's export and API surface in this group should be read with that in mind, and verified in the sandbox before it is designed against\.

## __Use cases__

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-035 · Import data in bulk__

__Actor__ Administrator · __Precondition__ A source file exists

__Main success scenario__

1. Administrator selects the target entity and uploads a file\.
2. The system validates every row without applying anything\.
3. The system presents a change set — creates, updates, retirements, rejections\.
4. Administrator reviews and confirms\.
5. The system applies the change set and reports the outcome per row\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. The file's columns do not match the entity → the import is refused before validation, naming the mismatch\. 3a\. Some rows are invalid → they are rejected by row number with a reason, and the remainder still import\. 3b\. The change set would delete a record in use → refused, and retirement is offered\. 4a\. Administrator declines → nothing is applied\.

__Postcondition__ Either the confirmed change set is applied and reported, or nothing changed and every rejection is named\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-036 · Export data__

__Actor__ Administrator or Technician · __Precondition__ Export permission

__Main success scenario__

1. The user selects an entity and any filters\.
2. The system generates an export containing every configured value, including those with no rows\.
3. Columns the user may not see are excluded, and the exclusion is stated\.
4. The file downloads\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. The export exceeds the size limit → it is queued and delivered on completion\. 3a\. The user lacks export\-PII → those columns are absent with a note\. 4a\. Export fails → the failure is reported, not silently truncated\.

__Postcondition__ The export is complete within the user's permission, and any reduction is visible\.

### __ISDT\-PRD1\-UC\-037 · Reconcile a migration__

__Actor__ Administrator, with the Data Architect · __Precondition__ An import has completed

__Main success scenario__

1. Administrator runs reconciliation for the imported entity\.
2. The system reports source count, imported count, rejected count and exceptions\.
3. Administrator reviews exceptions and resolves or accepts each\.
4. Reconciliation is recorded as complete with the accepted exception list\.

__Extensions__ — 2a\. Counts do not balance → reconciliation cannot be marked complete until every discrepancy is accounted for\. 3a\. An exception is accepted → the acceptance is recorded with actor and reason\.

__Postcondition__ Every source record is accounted for as imported, rejected, or deliberately excluded\. Nothing is unaccounted\.

## __Functional requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-157 to FR\-163 · Import, export, reconciliation and history 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-157 · Import framework__

__Description__ Common import behaviour that every entity\-specific import inherits\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Four requirements elsewhere specify imports — taxonomy \(FR\-037\), assets and software \(FR\-070\), users \(FR\-099\) and configuration\. They should behave identically, because an administrator who learns one import has learned them all\. The incumbent has __no bulk taxonomy import at all__ \(EV\-063\), so there is no existing pattern to inherit\.  
 __Source__ EV\-063, EV\-065, EV\-126 · C\-005, C\-006 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-065, Decision\) · __Applies to__ UC\-035

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST accept CSV and spreadsheet input for every importable entity\.  
 The system MUST validate every row __before applying anything__, and MUST present a change set distinguishing creates, updates, retirements and rejections\.  
 The system MUST apply nothing until the change set is confirmed\.  
 The system MUST reject an invalid row by row number with a reason, and MUST import the remainder\.  
 The system MUST refuse an import that would delete a record in use, offering retirement instead\.  
 Every import MUST write an audit entry naming the file, the actor and the counts \(FR\-150\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-467 Given a valid 500\-row file, when imported and confirmed, then 500 records exist and the audit records the counts\.  
 AC\-468 *\(negative\)* Given a file where rows 7, 22 and 108 are invalid, when imported, then those three are rejected by row number with reasons and the other 497 are created\.  
 AC\-469 *\(negative\)* Given a validated change set, when the administrator declines confirmation, then no record is created or altered\.  
 AC\-470 *\(negative\)* Given a file whose columns do not match the target entity, when uploaded, then it is refused before validation with the mismatch named\.  
 *Fixture* import\_framework\_seed — valid file, file with three invalid rows, file with mismatched columns\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The change set MUST be reviewable before confirmation without downloading anything\. A confirm button that applies an unseen change set is not a confirmation\. · __Data__ Writes target entity, Audit\. Imported files may contain PII and MUST NOT be retained beyond the import\. · __Telemetry__ import\_validated \{entity, rows, invalid\} · import\_applied \{created, updated, rejected\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-150 · __Surface__ admin, api · __Traces__ G\-005, C\-005, C\-006 → AC\-467, AC\-468, AC\-469, AC\-470 → M\-005

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-158 · Export framework__

__Description__ Every entity that can be imported can be exported\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ This is a Product Manager decision with a stated purpose: import and export both exist __so that a future migration away from this tool remains possible__ \(EV\-065\)\. Celestial is currently discovering what it costs to leave a tool whose export is partial — the report export omits unused values \(EV\-030\) and the user export is date\-range bounded \(EV\-125\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-030, EV\-065, EV\-125 · C\-005 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved \(EV\-065, Decision\) · __Applies to__ UC\-036

__Functional requirements__  
 Every entity supporting import MUST support export\. The set MUST be symmetric\.  
 An export MUST contain every configured value, including those with no rows \(FR\-118\)\.  
 An export MUST NOT be bounded by a date range unless the user requests one\. *This corrects *EV\-125*\.*  
 An export MUST be re\-importable into this system without transformation — the round trip MUST close\.  
 Columns excluded for permission reasons MUST be named in the output \(FR\-110\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-471 Given every importable entity, when the export list is opened, then all of them appear\.  
 AC\-472 Given an exported file, when re\-imported into an empty system, then the resulting records match the originals field for field\.  
 AC\-473 *\(negative\)* Given a user export with no date range requested, when run, then it returns every user and is not bounded by onboarding date\.  
 AC\-474 *\(negative\)* Given a user without export\-PII permission, when they export, then PII columns are absent and a note names them\.  
 *Fixture* export\_framework\_seed · *Verification* AC\-472 is the round\-trip test and is the strongest single check on G\-007\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A queued large export MUST notify on completion rather than requiring the user to wait\. · __Data__ Reads target entity\. Output may contain PII\. · __Telemetry__ export\_run \{entity, rows, columns\_excluded\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-118, FR\-110 · __Surface__ admin, api · __Traces__ G\-007, C\-005 → AC\-471, AC\-472, AC\-473, AC\-474 → M\-007

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-159 · Migration reconciliation__

__Description__ Proving nothing was lost\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ This is not greenfield — existing production data must migrate \(EV\-126, C\-006\)\. A migration nobody reconciled is a migration whose gaps are discovered months later by a user who cannot find their asset\.  
 __Source__ EV\-126, EV\-186 · C\-006 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ UC\-037

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST report, per migrated entity: source count, imported count, rejected count, deliberately excluded count, and the residual\.  
 Reconciliation MUST NOT be markable complete while the residual is non\-zero\.  
 Every deliberate exclusion MUST carry a reason and an actor\.  
 The reconciliation record MUST be permanent and MUST NOT be editable after completion\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-475 Given 680 source assets of which 668 import, 8 are rejected and 4 are deliberately excluded, when reconciliation runs, then the residual reads zero and it can be marked complete\.  
 AC\-476 *\(negative\)* Given 680 source assets and 668 imported with nothing else accounted for, when completion is attempted, then it is refused and the residual of 12 is stated\.  
 AC\-477 *\(negative\)* Given a completed reconciliation, when an administrator attempts to edit it, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-478 Given a deliberate exclusion, when the reconciliation record is opened, then its reason and actor appear\.  
 *Fixture* migration\_reconciliation\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The residual MUST be the most prominent figure on the screen; every other count is subordinate to it\. · __Data__ Writes Reconciliation record — permanent\. · __Telemetry__ reconciliation\_completed \{entity, source, imported, rejected, excluded\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-157 · __Surface__ admin · __Traces__ G\-005, C\-006 → AC\-475, AC\-476, AC\-477, AC\-478 → M\-005

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-160 · Ticket history migration__

__Description__ Bringing historical tickets across, if it is possible at all\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The administrator states that module export may suffice for assets but __not__ for Help Desk and Change, because resolutions and email conversations do not come across \(EV\-185\)\. The Frontend Engineer's fallback is explicit: migrate assets, start ticket history fresh \(EV\-186\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-185, EV\-186 · OQ\-002, OQ\-003 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-101 — __blocked__: feasibility depends on OQ\-002\) · __Applies to__ UC\-035, UC\-037

__Functional requirements__  
 Where historical tickets are migrated, the system MUST preserve reference, requester, category, status, dates, resolution and closure detail\.  
 Migrated tickets MUST be marked as migrated and MUST be distinguishable from tickets raised in this system\.  
 A migrated ticket MUST NOT be reopened or edited; it is a record, not live work\.  
 Where a requester cannot be matched, the ticket MUST attach to an archival identity \(FR\-099\) rather than being dropped\.  
 Where resolutions or conversations cannot be carried, the system MUST record that the migrated ticket is __partial__, naming what is missing\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-479 Given a migrated closed ticket, when it is opened, then it is marked migrated and no edit control renders\.  
 AC\-480 *\(negative\)* Given a migrated ticket, when reopening is attempted, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-481 Given a migrated ticket whose resolution could not be carried, when it is opened, then it is marked partial and the missing element is named\.  
 AC\-482 Given a migrated ticket whose requester matches no live user, when it is imported, then it attaches to an archival identity and is not rejected\.  
 *Fixture* migration\_tickets\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A partial migrated ticket MUST say what is missing; a ticket with an empty resolution field reads as a data\-quality failure rather than a migration limit\. · __Data__ Writes Ticket, History\. Confidential; free\-text content may contain PII\. · __Telemetry__ ticket\_migrated \{partial, archival\_requester\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-099, FR\-157 · __Traces__ G\-005 → AC\-479, AC\-480, AC\-481, AC\-482 → M\-005

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-161 · Attachment and conversation migration__

__Description__ The files and email threads attached to historical records\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ EV\-185 names email conversations specifically as what module export cannot carry\. Attachments are the other category — an asset agreement or an incident screenshot has evidential value, particularly for audit\.  
 __Source__ EV\-185, EV\-194 · OQ\-003 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-102 — __blocked__ on OQ\-003\) · __Applies to__ UC\-035

__Functional requirements__  
 Where attachments are migrated, the system MUST preserve filename, upload date and uploader\.  
 An attachment whose uploader cannot be matched MUST attach to an archival identity, not be dropped\.  
 A restricted attachment in the source MUST arrive restricted \(FR\-112\)\. It MUST NOT default to unrestricted\.  
 Where an attachment cannot be carried, the system MUST record a placeholder naming the filename and the reason, rather than leaving the record looking complete\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-483 Given a migrated ticket with two attachments, when it is opened, then both render with original filename and upload date\.  
 AC\-484 *\(negative\)* Given a source attachment marked confidential, when migrated, then it arrives restricted and an unpermitted technician receives 403\.  
 AC\-485 *\(negative\)* Given an attachment that could not be transferred, when the ticket is opened, then a placeholder names the file and the reason\.  
 *Fixture* migration\_attachments\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A placeholder MUST be visually distinct from a working attachment\. · __Data__ Writes Attachment\. __Restricted__ where marked; content unbounded and may contain PII\. · __Telemetry__ attachment\_migrated \{restricted, placeholder\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-112, FR\-160 · __Traces__ G\-005, C\-002 → AC\-483, AC\-484, AC\-485 → M\-005

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-162 · Import dry run__

__Description__ Rehearsing an import without consequences\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A 680\-row asset import applied wrongly is not easily undone, and the change set in FR\-157 shows what *would* happen but not what it *looks like* afterwards\. A dry run into an isolated state lets someone check the result before committing\. This also mirrors the client's own practice: production configuration cannot be altered without proper documentation, so changes are demonstrated in a sandbox \(EV\-148\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-148 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-103 — the sandbox practice is sourced; a dry\-run facility is not\) · __Applies to__ UC\-035

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST support a dry run that applies an import to an isolated state and reports the resulting records without altering live data\.  
 A dry run MUST NOT fire notifications, write history against live records, or consume identifiers\.  
 A dry run's results MUST be discardable and MUST be discarded automatically after a configurable period\.  
 The system MUST state clearly that a dry run is not a migration\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-486 Given a 100\-row dry run, when it completes, then results are viewable and no live record was created\.  
 AC\-487 *\(negative\)* Given a dry run, when it completes, then no notification was sent and no live history entry was written\.  
 AC\-488 *\(negative\)* Given a dry run that consumed no identifiers, when a live import then runs, then identifiers begin where they would have without the dry run\.  
 *Fixture* import\_framework\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield; isolation mechanism is an architecture decision\. · __UX__ Dry\-run results MUST be visually unmistakable from live data\. · __Data__ Isolated state, discarded on expiry\. · __Telemetry__ import\_dry\_run \{entity, rows\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-157 · __Surface__ admin · __Traces__ G\-005 → AC\-486, AC\-487, AC\-488 → M\-005

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-163 · Decommission readiness__

__Description__ Knowing when the incumbent can be switched off\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Licence cost is the entire quantified business case \(§7\.3\)\. The saving only begins when the incumbent's subscription ends, and that cannot happen until everything needed has been carried across and reconciled\. Without a readiness view the decision gets made on someone's recollection\.  
 __Source__ EV\-005, EV\-126, EV\-186 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-104 — designed; no source describes a decommission gate\) · __Applies to__ UC\-037

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST provide a readiness view listing every entity requiring migration with its reconciliation state\.  
 The view MUST distinguish entities reconciled complete, entities with an open residual, and entities deliberately not migrated\.  
 The view MUST NOT report readiness while any entity carries an open residual \(FR\-159\)\.  
 Deliberate non\-migration MUST require a recorded decision, naming who accepted the loss\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-489 Given assets reconciled complete and tickets deliberately not migrated with a recorded decision, when the readiness view is opened, then it reports ready and lists the accepted loss\.  
 AC\-490 *\(negative\)* Given one entity with an open residual, when the readiness view is opened, then it does not report ready and names that entity\.  
 AC\-491 *\(negative\)* Given an entity marked not\-migrated with no recorded decision, when the view is opened, then it is listed as unaccounted rather than accepted\.  
 *Fixture* migration\_reconciliation\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The view MUST be readable by someone who was not involved in the migration, since the person authorising decommission may not be\. · __Data__ Reads Reconciliation records\. · __Telemetry__ decommission\_readiness\_viewed \{ready, open\_residuals\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-159 · __Surface__ admin · __Traces__ G\-001, G\-005 → AC\-489, AC\-490, AC\-491 → M\-001, M\-005

# __16\. Security and access control__

Role definition is §15\.5 \(FR\-107, FR\-108\)\. Enforcement is §15\.7 \(FR\-135 – FR\-140\)\. This section covers what remains: __data classification, the PII inventory, residency, and the consolidated authorisation view__ — plus an honest disposition for the baseline controls that should be referenced rather than restated\.

__Legal clearance is not in place\.__ The evidence pack records three unanswered legal questions — whether the source product's terms permit automated inspection, whether design patents or trade dress protect the interface being replaced, and whether any client contract or NDA restricts the work\. All three are owned by the Security Lead and __none was answered within the evidence window__\. NG\-001 mitigates the second by not reproducing the interface\. The other two remain open\.

## __16\.1 Baseline controls — disposition__

TBD — the standing standards page does not exist | impact: baseline security controls \(encryption in transit and at rest, secret management, input validation, injection defence, rate limiting, dependency scanning, security logging\) cannot be referenced by ID and must not be restated here | owner: Security Lead \(A23–A26\) | required by: architecture gate | proposed default: publish the AI\-SDLC Project Requirements & Standards document to Confluence and cite its control IDs from each requirement's Data and security field \(P\-110\)\.

This is deliberate\. Restating generic controls in a PRD creates a second definition that drifts the moment the real one changes — the failure the context layer exists to prevent\. The requirements below are the ones genuinely specific to this product\.

## __16\.3 Requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-164 to FR\-168 · Classification, privacy, residency and authorisation 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-164 · Data classification enforcement__

__Description__ Classification is a property the system acts on, not a label in a document\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ A classification table nobody enforces is documentation\. Every export, notification and report already has a permission gate; classification is what tells those gates which fields matter\.  
 __Source__ EV\-189, EV\-194 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ All groups

__Functional requirements__  
 Every entity MUST carry a classification of Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted\.  
 Every field holding personal data MUST be flagged \(FR\-110\)\.  
 An unclassified entity MUST NOT be creatable — the schema MUST refuse it\.  
 Export, notification and report behaviour MUST derive from classification rather than from per\-surface configuration\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-492 *\(negative\)* Given a new entity added with no classification, when the schema is validated in CI, then it fails and names the entity\.  
 AC\-493 Given a field flagged personal, when it is exported by a user without export\-PII, then it is absent \(FR\-110\)\.  
 AC\-494 Given the data map report, when run, then every entity and every flagged field appears\.  
 *Fixture* privacy\_marking\_seed · *Verification* AC\-492 is a schema assertion in CI, not a UI test\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ A Restricted field MUST be visually marked wherever it is displayed\. · __Data__ Field and entity metadata\. · __Telemetry__ classification\_gate\_applied \{surface, fields\_excluded\} · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-492, AC\-493, AC\-494 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-165 · PII inventory and lawful basis__

__Description__ A derivable answer to "what personal data does this system hold, and why"\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent supports PII and ePHI marking, anonymisation and erasure \(EV\-194\), which implies someone once needed to answer this question\. Whether ePHI applies to an internal service desk at all is __unestablished__ — no session mentioned health data — and is registered as OQ\-105\.  
 __Source__ EV\-194 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-111 — no lawful\-basis determination exists\) · __Applies to__ All groups

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST produce a data map listing every entity, every flagged field, its classification and its retention position\.  
 The map MUST be derived from schema metadata, not maintained by hand\.  
 Each personal\-data field MUST carry a lawful basis, or be flagged as having none recorded\.  
 The map MUST be exportable for an audit or a privacy review\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-495 Given the data map, when run, then it lists every entity from §16\.2 with its flagged fields\.  
 AC\-496 *\(negative\)* Given a personal\-data field with no lawful basis recorded, when the map is run, then it is listed as basis\-not\-recorded rather than omitted\.  
 AC\-497 Given a new personal field added to any entity, when the map is regenerated, then it appears without anyone editing the map\.  
 *Fixture* privacy\_marking\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The map MUST be readable by a privacy reviewer who does not know the schema\. · __Data__ Metadata only; the map itself holds no personal data\. · __Telemetry__ data\_map\_generated \{entities, pii\_fields, basis\_missing\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-110, FR\-164 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-495, AC\-496, AC\-497 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-166 · Data residency__

__Description__ Where the data physically sits\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ The incumbent is a multi\-tenant cloud hosted in the vendor's India region \(EV\-019\)\. The replacement deploys initially on AWS with later migration to Azure to satisfy a Microsoft specialization audit \(EV\-077, C\-011\)\. Sites include __Canada__ \(EV\-019\), so a cross\-border question exists whether or not anyone has raised it\.  
 __Source__ EV\-019, EV\-077 · C\-011 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-112 — OQ\-025 means the hosting plan is outstanding\) · __Applies to__ All groups

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST record its deployment region and make it visible to an administrator\.  
 The system MUST NOT replicate personal data outside the declared region without an explicit configured exception\.  
 A change of region MUST be a recorded decision, not a deployment side effect\.  
 Where a site's jurisdiction imposes a residency constraint, the system MUST be able to state whether it is met\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-498 Given a deployed system, when an administrator opens the system information view, then the deployment region is stated\.  
 AC\-499 *\(negative\)* Given no configured exception, when a backup or replica target outside the declared region is configured, then it is refused\.  
 AC\-500 Given a region change, when it completes, then it appears in the configuration audit with actor and date \(FR\-150\)\.  
 *Fixture* residency\_config\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield; the AWS\-then\-Azure path is C\-011 and belongs to the architecture gate\. · __UX__ Region MUST be visible without reading infrastructure configuration\. · __Data__ Configuration\. · __Telemetry__ residency\_declared \{region\} · __Traces__ C\-011 → AC\-498, AC\-499, AC\-500 → M\-006

__Canada is the live question here\.__ Nothing in the evidence addresses whether Canadian employee data may be held in an India or a general\-purpose region\. Nobody asked, and the absence of a complaint is not clearance\. Registered as OQ\-151, owned by the Security Lead\.

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-167 · Consolidated role\-to\-capability matrix__

__Description__ One place that answers "who can do what"\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Permissions are specified across ten groups\. Without a consolidated view, nobody — least of all the Security Lead at G2 — can see the whole picture, and the incumbent's failure mode was roles whose permissions __could not even be viewed__ \(EV\-187\)\.  
 __Source__ EV\-187, EV\-188, EV\-189 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ All groups

__Functional requirements__  
 The system MUST render a single matrix of every role against every module and named permission\.  
 The matrix MUST be generated from enforced permissions, not maintained separately — it MUST be impossible for it to disagree with behaviour\.  
 The matrix MUST be exportable for audit\.  
 Every named permission enforced anywhere MUST appear \(FR\-136\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-501 Given six roles and the full permission set, when the matrix is opened, then every role\-permission pair is shown as granted or not\.  
 AC\-502 *\(negative\)* Given a permission enforced in code but absent from the matrix, when CI runs, then it fails and names the permission\.  
 AC\-503 Given a permission removed from a role, when the matrix is regenerated, then it reflects the change with no separate edit\.  
 *Fixture* permissions\_seed, roles\_seed · *Verification* AC\-502 compares enforced permissions to the matrix in CI — the same check as AC\-402\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The matrix MUST be readable at a glance for a single role, since that is how it will actually be used\. · __Data__ Reads Role\. · __Telemetry__ permission\_matrix\_viewed · __Prerequisites__ FR\-107, FR\-136 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-501, AC\-502, AC\-503 → M\-006

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-168 · Authorisation invariants__

__Description__ Rules that hold across every module, tested once rather than per feature\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Access\-control defects appear at seams\. The incumbent's private report invisible to the super admin \(EV\-151\) and its renamed\-report visibility leak \(EV\-152\) are both seam failures — neither module was wrong on its own\.  
 __Source__ EV\-151, EV\-152, EV\-189 · C\-002 · __Priority__ P0 · __Status__ Approved · __Applies to__ All groups

__Functional requirements__  
 No surface — web, API, export, scheduled delivery, notification — MAY return a record the requester's role and scope exclude \(FR\-135, FR\-127, FR\-144\)\.  
 No lower\-privileged actor MAY conceal a record from a higher\-privileged one \(FR\-119\)\.  
 No permission MAY be granted implicitly by a related permission; grants MUST be additive and explicit \(FR\-136\)\.  
 Every bulk operation MUST permission\-check per record, never per batch \(FR\-007\)\.  
 These invariants MUST be tested as a suite, independently of the features that rely on them\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-504 Given one out\-of\-scope record and a scoped user, when it is requested through web, API, export, report and scheduled delivery in turn, then all five refuse identically\.  
 AC\-505 *\(negative\)* Given a private report owned by a technician, when an administrator lists reports, then it appears — no lower actor conceals from a higher one\.  
 AC\-506 *\(negative\)* Given a role with ticket\-edit but not ticket\-delete, when a delete is attempted, then it is refused; edit does not imply delete\.  
 AC\-507 *\(negative\)* Given a bulk operation over 50 records of which 5 are out of scope, when it runs, then those 5 are refused individually and 45 succeed\.  
 *Fixture* permissions\_seed, reports\_visibility\_seed, incidents\_bulk\_101 · *Verification* This is a standing invariant suite, run on every build, not a per\-feature test\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ — · __Data__ Reads Role, User, target entities\. · __Telemetry__ invariant\_suite\_run \{passed, failed\} · __Prerequisites__ FR\-135 · __Traces__ C\-002 → AC\-504, AC\-505, AC\-506, AC\-507 → M\-006

# __17\. Accessibility__

__No evidence exists for this section\.__ Across nine hours and 203 facts, __accessibility was never mentioned__ — not as a requirement, not as a constraint, not as a question\. There is no designer on the roster \(OQ\-101\) and no accessibility accountability was named by any speaker\.

Every requirement below is therefore a proposal\. The conformance target in particular is chosen, not sourced\. This section exists because shipping an internal tool that some employees cannot use is a real harm, and because H4 rejects a PRD with no accessibility target — not because anyone asked for it\.

## __17\.1 Conformance target__

__Proposed: WCAG 2\.2 Level AA__ \(P\-113\)\. Rationale: it is the current recognised baseline for an employee\-facing web application, and Celestial already operates under an ISO regime that expects stated standards rather than best effort\. If a different target is preferred, or if a legal obligation applies in Canada or India that dictates one, that decision replaces this proposal — see OQ\-152\.

## __17\.2 Requirements__

![](data:image/png;base64,)FR\-169 to FR\-174 · Accessibility 

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-169 · Keyboard operability__

__Description__ Every function reachable without a pointing device\.  
 __Source__ None — proposed · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-113\) · __Applies to__ all\_with\_surface: web — affects every use case with a web surface

__Functional requirements__  
 Every interactive control MUST be reachable and operable by keyboard alone\.  
 Tab order MUST follow visual and logical reading order\.  
 No interaction MUST require a hover state to be discoverable\.  
 A keyboard trap MUST NOT exist in any dialog, including the export and closure dialogs\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-508 Given the incident list, when a user tabs through it, then every control including Pick Up is reachable in DOM order\.  
 AC\-509 *\(negative\)* Given the closure dialog, when a user tabs to its end, then focus returns within the dialog and does not escape to the page behind\.  
 AC\-510 *\(negative\)* Given any control revealed only on hover, when the interface is audited, then none exists\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_queue\_seed · *Verification* Automated axe\-core scan plus a manual keyboard pass per release\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __Data__ None\. · __Telemetry__ None\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-508, AC\-509, AC\-510 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-170 · Focus visibility and management__

__Description__ Always knowing where you are\.  
 __Source__ None — proposed · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-113\) · __Applies to__ all\_with\_surface: web

__Functional requirements__  
 Focus MUST be visible on every focusable element, at the conformance target's contrast minimum\.  
 Opening a dialog MUST move focus into it; closing MUST return focus to the invoking control\.  
 An asynchronous update — a queue refreshing on assignment \(FR\-013\) — MUST NOT move focus\.  
 A validation failure MUST move focus to the first field named\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-511 Given the export dialog opened from the incident list, when it closes, then focus returns to the export control\.  
 AC\-512 *\(negative\)* Given a user typing in the queue filter, when another technician assigns a ticket and the queue updates, then focus does not move\.  
 AC\-513 Given a submission refused for an empty description, when the refusal renders, then focus is on the description field\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_queue\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-511, AC\-512, AC\-513 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-171 · Screen reader semantics__

__Description__ The interface conveys meaning without sight\.  
 __Source__ None — proposed · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-113\) · __Applies to__ all\_with\_surface: web

__Functional requirements__  
 Every control MUST have an accessible name; an icon\-only control MUST carry a label\.  
 Status, priority and state MUST NOT be conveyed by colour alone — the green\-and\-orange stage rendering in FR\-077 MUST carry text or an icon too\.  
 A status change MUST be announced through a live region\.  
 Tables MUST use real table semantics with header association\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-514 Given the change stage bar, when read by a screen reader, then followed and bypassed stages are distinguishable without colour\.  
 AC\-515 *\(negative\)* Given every icon\-only control, when audited, then none lacks an accessible name\.  
 AC\-516 Given a ticket moving to Resolved, when the change renders, then it is announced\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_status\_seed, changes\_stages\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ This constrains Diagram 12's colour scheme directly\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-514, AC\-515, AC\-516 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-172 · Contrast and text sizing__

__Description__ Legibility\.  
 __Source__ None — proposed · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-113\) · __Applies to__ all\_with\_surface: web

__Functional requirements__  
 Text and interface components MUST meet the conformance target's contrast ratios\.  
 The interface MUST remain usable at 200% zoom with no loss of function and no horizontal scrolling at standard widths\.  
 Text MUST NOT be presented as an image of text\.  
 The theme inheritance required in FR\-001's UX field MUST NOT reduce contrast below the target\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-517 Given every text and component pairing, when scanned, then all meet the target contrast ratio\.  
 AC\-518 Given the incident detail at 200% zoom, when used, then every function remains available without horizontal scrolling\.  
 *Fixture* — · *Verification* Automated contrast scan per build, plus a zoom pass per release\.

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-517, AC\-518 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-173 · Mobile browser usability__

__Description__ Usable on a phone browser, without being a mobile app\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ NG\-008 excludes a native mobile application — the incumbent published one for iOS and Android and it is unused \(EV\-052\)\. But excluding an app is not excluding phones, and a requester reporting a broken laptop may well be on one\.  
 __Source__ EV\-052 · NG\-008 · __Priority__ P2 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-114\) · __Applies to__ UC\-001, UC\-005, UC\-008, UC\-011

__Functional requirements__  
 The requester journeys — raise, confirm, approve, acknowledge — MUST be usable on a mobile browser\.  
 Touch targets on those journeys MUST meet the conformance target's minimum size\.  
 Technician and administrator surfaces are __not__ required to be mobile\-usable; that is an explicit non\-requirement, not an oversight\.  
 An emailed approval or acknowledgement link MUST work on a mobile browser \(FR\-043, FR\-068\)\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-519 Given a mobile browser at 375px width, when a requester raises an incident, then the journey completes with no horizontal scrolling\.  
 AC\-520 Given an emailed approval link opened on a phone, when the approver approves, then it succeeds\.  
 AC\-521 *\(negative\)* Given the technician queue on a 375px viewport, when opened, then it is not required to be usable and states that a larger screen is recommended\.  
 *Fixture* approvals\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __UX__ The recommendation in AC\-521 MUST be advisory, not a block\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-519, AC\-520, AC\-521 → M\-004

#### __ISDT\-PRD1\-FR\-174 · Error identification__

__Description__ Failures that can be understood and fixed\.  
 __Use case and benefits__ Roughly forty acceptance criteria across this PRD require a refusal to __name the field__ or __state the reason__\. This requirement makes that a single accessibility obligation rather than forty independent behaviours\.  
 __Source__ Derived from FR\-001, FR\-027, FR\-085 and others · __Priority__ P1 · __Status__ __Proposed__ \(P\-113\) · __Applies to__ all\_with\_surface: web

__Functional requirements__  
 Every validation failure MUST identify the field in text, associated programmatically with that field\.  
 An error MUST NOT be conveyed by colour or position alone\.  
 An error summary MUST list every failure at once, not one at a time\.  
 An error message MUST state what to do, not only what is wrong\.

__Acceptance criteria__  
 AC\-522 Given a form with three empty mandatory fields, when submitted, then all three are named in one summary and each is associated with its field\.  
 AC\-523 *\(negative\)* Given a validation error, when read by a screen reader, then the field and reason are conveyed without relying on colour\.  
 AC\-524 Given a refused closure, when the message renders, then it names the missing field and what to supply\.  
 *Fixture* incidents\_closure\_seed

__Technical__ Not applicable — greenfield\. · __Traces__ G\-004 → AC\-522, AC\-523, AC\-524 → M\-004

# __18\. Internationalisation__

Not applicable — English only\. Celestial operates three sites: Bangalore, Noida/NCR and Canada \(EV\-019, C\-008\)\. Every session, document and artefact in the evidence base is in English, and no source raised language as a requirement, a constraint or a question\.

__One thing makes this disposition less safe than it looks\.__ One of the three sites is in __Canada__, where language obligations can attach to employee\-facing systems depending on province\. Nobody raised it, and the absence of a complaint is not clearance\.

The disposition therefore stands as written, but it is flagged as OQ\-153 for the Security Lead and Executive Sponsor rather than closed\. If French is required, this section becomes real work — string externalisation, pluralisation, date and number formats, and translated notification templates \(FR\-142\) — and it is far cheaper to know that now than after 163 requirements are built\.

What is retained regardless of the answer: __date and time handling__ must respect per\-site operational hours, holidays and time zones \(FR\-106, FR\-030\)\. That is not internationalisation; it is C\-008, and it is already specified\.

# __19\. AI evaluation criteria__

Not applicable — there is no AI capability in this product\.

§12 declares product AI usage as __None__\. No model call, no generated content, no autonomous decision appears anywhere in 163 requirements\. The two places one might expect it are deliberately deterministic:

- __Priority derivation__ \(FR\-009\) is a configurable matrix, not a classifier \(EV\-054\)\.
- __Article suggestion__ \(FR\-048\) matches on category association, not on semantic similarity\.

The AI overlay therefore does not apply\. No evaluation set, no accuracy or groundedness threshold, no hallucination rate, no adversarial suite and no model\-version re\-trigger rule is required — because there is no model to evaluate\.

__What would change this\.__ Reopening NG\-003 \(the MCP conversational interface proposed as a longer\-term nice\-to\-have at EV\-035\), or introducing auto\-categorisation, semantic search over ticket text, or suggested resolutions\. Any of those activates the AI overlay, and __§19 must be authored before that capability can pass G2__\. That is a change request under change\-request, not an amendment to this PRD\.

AI usage *in development* — this pipeline — remains declared at Medium in §12 and is governed by the standards page, not by this section\.

# __20\. Non\-functional requirements__

__Read this before reading any number below\.__

__Nothing in 203 facts gives a ticket volume\.__ Not per day, not per week, not per month\. Registered as OQ\-102 since the front matter and now blocking in four separate places\. Every latency, throughput and capacity figure in this section is therefore a __proposal__ \(P\-120\), and the Architect should not size against them\.

Three figures here *are* derivable and are marked as such: launch data volumes \(§14\.2\), asset turnover from the four\-year replacement policy \(BR\-006\), and two intervals already specified as requirements \(FR\-003 mail polling, FR\-098 directory sync\)\.

__The one screenshot that would fix most of this__ is the incumbent's 20\-day received\-versus\-completed dashboard widget \(EV\-008, FR\-124\)\.

## __22\.1 What this PRD contributes to testing__

__Contribution__

__Detail__

__524 acceptance criteria__

Every one in Given / When / Then form with a single assertion and a named fixture\. This is the direct input to test\-generate\.

__~200 negative, boundary and failure criteria__

Every requirement carries at least one\. §15\.7 has the highest ratio at 21 of 40, which is appropriate for access control\.

__~90 named fixtures__

Shared across groups where the same data state serves several requirements\. A fixture named in more than one group is deliberately the same fixture\.

__Tests requiring more than a UI driver__

Clock manipulation: AC\-058, AC\-073, AC\-144, AC\-173, AC\-203, AC\-310, AC\-360, AC\-387, AC\-430, AC\-464\. Fault injection: AC\-438\. Concurrency: AC\-040, AC\-165\. Schema and route assertions in CI: AC\-183, AC\-384, AC\-385, AC\-402, AC\-444, AC\-492, AC\-502\. Network inspection: AC\-368\. Performance harness: AC\-215, AC\-525\.

__Standing invariant suite__

FR\-168 requires the authorisation invariants to be tested independently of the features relying on them — a suite, run every build, not a set of per\-feature tests\.

__Accessibility verification__

Automated scan per build plus a manual keyboard and zoom pass per release \(FR\-169 – FR\-174\)\. __No one currently owns this__ \(OQ\-154\)\.

## __22\.2 Risk\-ranked areas__

Where testing effort should concentrate, ranked by consequence of failure rather than by requirement count:

1. __Authorisation and scoping__ \(FR\-135, FR\-127, FR\-137, FR\-168\) — both of the incumbent's known access\-control defects were seam failures\. Highest consequence, lowest visibility\.
2. __History integrity__ \(FR\-147, FR\-149\) — compliance\-bearing and explicitly mandated \(EV\-088\)\. AC\-438 requires fault injection: a change must not persist if its history entry fails\.
3. __SLA calculation__ \(FR\-030, FR\-021, FR\-049\) — working hours, holidays, pauses and approval latency compound\. Easy to get subtly wrong, hard to notice\.
4. __Bulk operations__ \(FR\-007, FR\-016, FR\-092\) — per\-record permission checks, partial failure reporting, and the 100\-record ceiling that is G\-002 in its entirety\.
5. __Migration__ \(FR\-157 – FR\-163\) — one\-shot, hard to reverse, and reconciliation is the only proof it worked\.
